Sources indicate that walmart appears to have dropped support for Apple Pay on its website and in its iPhone app. This comes just a few weeks after the retailer finally added support for Apple’s payment platform to its app and website.

It has been revealed that 9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Now, she’s dropping the official version of the track exclusively on Amazon Music.

Like her album you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love, the two holiday songs capture different sides of love and romance: “Take Me Home (4 Christmas)” is an upbeat, enthusiastic track, inspired by Christmas songs from the Eighties as Rodrigo sings about the anticipation of meeting a significant other’s family. A playful video starred SNL cast member Ben Marshall as the guy bringing her home for Christmas, while Cynthia Nixon took on the role of Marshall’s mom meeting Rodrigo for the first time.

“Miss This Christmas” is a sadder, melancholy ballad, written about longing for someone during the holiday season. “Happy Christmas to the lonely/Broken hearts that feel just like me,” she sings on the track, which she wrote with Dan Nigro and Amy Allen. “Yeah, next year’s gonna look real different/Tell your folks I’ll miss their Christmas.”.

Industry observers note that when Rodrigo performed “Miss This Christmas” at Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena this week, she called it a “really sad Christmas song” and shared that “no one’s ever really heard it before.” Two days before that, she’d stopped by Jack White’s Blue Room in the city, recording two 20-minute sets for a live-to-acetate session for Third Man Records. Black Friday isn't until November 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday 2026 sale is already bringing some decent discounts on TP-Link routers, with prices starting at $44.99 and savings of up to $100. The deals cover quite a few different networking needs, from compact travel routers that let you connect multiple devices to hotel wifi to more powerful home routers designed for faster internet intends and households with lots of connected devices.

According to recent reports, TP-Link’s Roam routers are compact enough to travel with and let you share a hotel or public internet connection across your devices through a private Wi-Fi network—and right now, Amazon has three models on sale: the Roam 6 AX1500 for $44.99 (was $59.99), the Roam 6 AX3000 for $55.98 (was $79.99), and the Roam 7 BE3600 for $87.99 (was $119.99). All three support VPN connections and multiple operating modes, with the main differences coming down to speed. The AX1500 offers up to 1.5Gbps, the AX3000 doubles that and adds a 2.5Gbps WAN port, while the Wi-Fi 7-enabled Roam 7 reaches up to 3.6Gbps.

Recent findings suggest that the TP-Link Archer AX21 V5 AX1800 is down to $54.99 from $89.99, saving you $35 on an affordable Wi-Fi 6 router for everyday home use. Its dual-band connection offers combined theoretical speeds of up to 1.8Gbps, which should be sufficient for typical activities like streaming, video calls, and browsing across several devices.

Industry observers note that for homes with faster internet aims, multiple gamers, or lots of connected devices, TP-Link's Archer BE700 and BE770 offer tri-band Wi-Fi 7, including access to the 6GHz band for compatible devices. Both support EasyMesh for extended coverage and have 10Gbps WAN ports, although the BE770 provides faster wireless speeds and more wired connectivity. As for pricing, the TP-Link Archer BE700 is down to $248 from $349.99, saving you just over $100. It offers theoretical speeds of up to 15Gbps, a 2.5Gbps LAN port, and three Gigabit LAN ports. For just $52 more, the Archer BE770 (now $299.99, was $369.99) bumps speeds up to 18Gbps and adds a dedicated 10Gbps LAN port, making it better suited to high-speed network storage and large file transfers.

The TP-Link Deco BE25 is down to $99.98 from $129.99, saving you $30 on a Wi-Fi 7 router designed to work as part of a mesh network. It offers dual-band wireless speeds of up to 5Gbps, two 2.5Gbps Ethernet ports, and AI-driven roaming that helps connected devices switch between Deco units as you move around your home.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

It has been revealed that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Tech Report: Latest Gemini setting lets you keep chat history, but turn off AI training [U]

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (432 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google is rolling out new privacy settings for the Gemini app that will let you “keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training.”.
  • It has been revealed that revision 11/24: This new setting is now widely rolling out.
  • Under “Help train generative AI models with,” you’ll find the upcoming “Chat content including text & attachments” setting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is rolling out new privacy settings for the Gemini app that will let you “keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training.”.

It has been revealed that revision 11/24: This new setting is now widely rolling out. On gemini.google.com, tap the settings gear icon to find a new “Gemini History” item at the very bottom. This opens myactivity.google.com/product/gemini with an On/Off dropdown.

Under “Help train generative AI models with,” you’ll find the upcoming “Chat content including text & attachments” setting. It’s enabled by default.

Your future chats won’t be used to train generative AI models, unless you provide feedback.

Training on “Audio and Gemini Live videos & screenshares” remains an opt-in preference.

Original 11/16: Gemini’s existing Keep Activity setting “controls how long your chats are saved and whether they are used to train generative AI models.”.

Google is now separating that preference into two new options.

It has been revealed that this is huge. One of the major things Siri-AI customers on iPhone like to point out is that while their assistant is a less capable portmanteau of Siri and Gemini, their queries are not used for AI training. Gemini on Android, on the other hand, offers the superior AI platform with the caveat that there is no way to opt out of training and still retain your chat history. Until now. Now users of Gemini on Android get the best of both worlds - the best of Google's AI models powering their AI experiences and their chat history siloed from AI training.

The first setting is called “History” and lets you “control how long your history is saved.” If disabled:.

“…future chats will be saved for around 2 months and used to respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its users, and the public, with help from human reviewers.”.

The duration is currently 24 hours for chat context, and 72 hours to help protect Google, consumers, and the public.

The second setting allows you to “separately control whether your chat content, including text and attachments, is used to train generative AI models.”.

With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training.

If Keep Activity is currently off, the two “new settings will both be off.” These changes are rolling out over the “coming weeks,” and Google is notifying owners via email.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, R ob Gronkowski is in a familiar place as magic hour concedes to Friday-night lights in Los Angeles.
  • The future Hall of Famer tight end is crew-cutted and cut.
  • He has the full attention of the gathered players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, R ob Gronkowski is in a familiar place as magic hour concedes to Friday-night lights in Los Angeles. He is pacing in a locker room on the campus of Sierra Canyon School, a high school that counts various Jenners and LeBron James’ sons among its alumni.

The future Hall of Famer tight end is crew-cutted and cut. At 37, he is just five months older than Travis Kelce, who is still hauling in touchdowns from Patrick Mahomes, and he still looks like he could grab six catches for 107 yards and two TDs. Alas, Gronk — like Jesus and Cher, he goes by one name — exited the game at 33 with four Super Bowl rings.

He has the full attention of the gathered players. Gronk hits all of his marks in his pregame talk. Be accountable. Trust your teammates. Make the play. “You’re going to remember Friday-night football games for the rest of your lives,” indicates Gronk.

He speaks in a cadence that, for the clueless, suggests a brain pan both punch-drunk and super high.

According to recent reports, gronk gets serious, or as serious as someone named Gronk can get. He talks of injuries — Gronk lost a college season to back problems and major parts of his NFL career to a list of injuries that reads like the medical chart of a guy who got T-boned by a Ford F-150 while driving a Nissan Versa.

In a recent development, “If you’re injured, you can’t participate,” indicates Gronk. “You’re worthless to the team. You gotta take care of your body. You gotta rehab hard.”.

Recent findings suggest that “And speaking of that, we’re talking DNA Vibe,” states Gronk. “It’s a jazz band and consists of red-light therapy. It has vibrational frequency on it, too. And every single one of you here in this room on this team is getting one. Use the jazz band; it works to help the healing process naturally in your body.”.

Sources indicate that the players look confused. No matter. Gronk finishes up.

“Thank you for having me, and kick some ass!”.

Sources indicate that “There’s different levels of being yourself. I’m not gonna tell ‘69’ jokes on tv — no chance.”.

Recent findings suggest that I’m scheduled to talk with Gronk the next afternoon at the Waldorf Astoria Beverly Hills. That morning, I look up the product he mentioned the night before. It has the cumber­some official name of DNA Vibe Jazz Band and has nothing to do with learning to play bebop during fifth period at Millard Fillmore Junior High and everything to do with helping you recover from injuries while using red-light therapy that I do not understand. You may not be surprised to learn that Gronkowski is DNA Vibe Jazz Band’s primary spokesman. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

At the hotel, Gronk happily shakes my hand, his massive forearms covered by matching bandages.

“I get really dehydrated when I travel, so I get an IV,” states Gronk. “I also got ozone therapy, where it takes out the blood and then you put ozone in it.”.

In a recent development, I smile as if I have even the smallest idea of what the hell he is talking about. I try to move to more familiar ground. I’m about to ask him about his role on the top-rated Fox NFL Sunday pregame show when a bushy-haired man approaches us. Gronk makes the introduction.

The guy is serial entrepreneur Lance Collins, who co-founded the sports-drink firm BodyArmor, whose remaining 85 percent Coca-Cola bought for $5.6 billion in 2021. (The soft-drink company bought the first 15 percent in 2018.) Gronk’s endorsement deal included equity, earning him a big payout. Collins and Gronk are now on to another sports drink.

According to recent reports, there are celeb endorsers who observe a firewall between a theoretically journalistic interview and hawking products. That’s not Gronk. Related Content Olivia Rodrigo Drops Official Version of Melancholy ‘Miss This Christmas’ on Amazon Music Watch Miranda Lambert Perform Medley of Her Hits at Dallas Cowboys Halftime Show Lola Blankets' Black Friday Sale Is Officially Live — and Everything Is 50% Off 'Hejira' at 50: Beck, Cameron Crowe, Clairo, and More Honor Joni Mitchell's 1976 Masterpiece.

In a recent development, “Put it in the story,” notes Gronkowski. “Come on, let’s put it in the story.”.

I ask what the drink is called.

Recent findings suggest that “Recover 180,” Gronk repeats. “It’s an organic sports drink, and it’s filled with electrolytes.”.

Industry observers note that gronk calls the drink delicious and tasty. Collins suggests “delicious and nutritious,” an improvement, and Gronk instantly repeats the revised copy.

I’m beginning to think Collins being in the lobby is not coincidental.

Industry observers note that collins pulls out his phone and begins showing me ads for the drink. He only stops after I theatrically look at my watch for a third time. “I’m gonna make a ton of money, and he’ll make a lot of money,” indicates Collins. He mentions he has a tequila line that also features Gronk.

“We’re in on everything!” claims Gronk.

According to recent reports, rob Gronkowski was the rare tight end who could pancake a linebacker on one play and then one-hand a pass from Tom Brady in the end zone on the next. All of this while partying his ass off, often with his four brothers and, sometimes, his dad, who built a state-of-the-art weight room in the family basement for his boys. They all had stints as pro athletes. The Brothers Gronk liked to prank one another with stunts like throwing forks at each other hard enough to lodge in someone’s elbow. And then there was the time at the oldest brother’s Vegas bachelor party that one of them — or someone in their crew — took a dump in a chip bag. Their dates were unamused. (I learned all of this while reading his memoir, It’s Good to Be Gronk, a not-exactly-Nabokovian account of his salad days.).

But that’s all in the past. Gronkowski has now lined up for the next trick play: erasing the line between sincerity and commerce with his buffoonish charm. It is both impressive and a bit icky.

It has been revealed that longtime friend and former Fresh England Patriots teammate Julian Edelman says it’s all about his work ethic. According to Edelman, Gronk arrives on time and knows his lines better than anyone on commercial shoots.

“I’m a slapdick compared to Rob Gronkowski.”.

OK! Welcome to the Gronk Industrial Complex. Keep your head on a swivel or you’re gonna get blindsided.

Industry observers note that from the start, Gronk understood something that many famous dudes never do: Shtick is tolerated, but only after brilliance has been established. Like Dennis Rodman and Tom Cruise before him, Gronk knows the world will let you be a total weirdo if you perform like a superstar. But before you jump on the proverbial Oprah’s couch you must — in Gronk terminology — kick some ass.

Here’s a Gronk creation story. Edelman was in his second year with the Patriots when Gronkowski arrived from the University of Arizona, where he lived in an off-campus house with a hot tub in the front yard. But Edelman didn’t see that side of Gronk in their first training camp together. Initially, Gronk grinded away at the playbook and impressed head coach Bill Belichick with his dominant blocking.

Then the team broke camp and Edelman saw Gronk Unchained. A bunch of players hit a nightclub, and within minutes there was the real Gronk.

“When someone states, ‘I thought this guy was going to be an idiot,’ I just start laughing.”.

It has been revealed that “He’s dancing in the middle of the dance floor, going crazy, having the time of his life, being Gronk,” remembers Edelman. “And I walk in, and I’m like, ‘Oh, my God, what is this guy doing?’ Rob comes over, and there’s a waiter walking by, and the waiter has a bunch of drinks and finger food. Gronk just grabs a handful of shrimp and eats the shrimp. He’s like, ‘What’s up, Jules?’ And I’m like, ‘Oh, my God, what is this?’”.

Let it be noted that Gronk did not grab the shrimp until he demonstrated his value.

Sources indicate that “No one could say anything because of how hard he worked and his production,” notes Edelman. “Even the coaching staff — they’re like, ‘Well, that’s just fucking Gronk. If he’s going to score three touchdowns and be the point of attack for our running game, then whatever he does, we don’t care.’”.

Bill Bradley was a legendary basketball player and one-time presidential candidate who shares nothing in common with Gronk. Bradley once said domination on the court and life depended on situational awareness.

“You develop a sense of where you are,” stated Bradley.

Recent findings suggest that that’s Gronk. Here’s an example. For his entire public life, Gronk has made “69” jokes, with the legend being he once bought $69,000 of Apple stock in 2014 on the recommendation of his contractor, and then forgot about it for years. (Depending on when he bought it, that $69,000 would be worth roughly a million dollars today if it wasn’t sold.).

I ask him if it is hard for him to rein in his inner 69 on the Fox pregame show, which is decidedly G-rated.

“There’s different levels of being yourself, 100 percent,” says Gronk. “I’m not gonna tell the ‘69’ jokes on TV — no chance.” He smiles his goofy smile.

“But a podcast or something, that’s the place to say all those types of jokes.”.

He also knows not to bite the hand that feeds him. I ask him if he is worried about the impact of CTE, a degenerative brain disease linked to repeated blows to the head. He dissembles with the skill of a tobacco lobbyist.

“You hear all the studies about CTE, and there’s a lot of science behind it,” indicates Gronk. “You’ve got to believe in the science, but it’s still kind of a myth as well, because how can you truly pinpoint anything to football?”.

Recent findings suggest that to the casual observer, Gronk comes across as a cartoon character with a caveman name. That’s how he likes it.

Recent findings suggest that “The best position I love to be in is when I’m underestimated,” indicates Gronk as he exchanges a bro handshake with his IV guy. “When someone says, ‘I thought this guy was going to be an idiot,’ I just start laughing.”.

Gronk puts on his serious face.

“That’s when I know that that person is truly an idiot.”.

Sources indicate that the next day, Gronkowski arrives just after 6 a.m. at the Fox NFL Sunday studio. He’s the kid on the show — 18 years younger than Michael Strahan, 29 years younger than Howie Long, and more than 40 years younger than Terry Bradshaw, all Hall of Famers. Still, he seems to have the lowest energy level of the bunch when they emerge for a run-through shortly after 7 a.m. Maybe it’s the crimson-checked suit and tie he had to don. The entire panel is wearing suits from the Collection by Michael Strahan (available at JCPenney).

The atmosphere before airtime feels less like a billion-dollar television property than the greenroom at a 55-and-over-community talent show. Bradshaw sings snatches of Marty Robbins’ “Big Iron,” a country & western song released in 1959. Turns out Strahan knows the song from his dad. The two sing the chorus: “And he’s here to do some business/With the big iron on his hip/Big iron …”.

It has been revealed that long looks on like an anthropologist studying an ancient and backward tribe. Gronk doesn’t seem to notice, his head buried in his cue cards, trying to memorize the points he wants to make. A few minutes later, Bradshaw tries to knock the cue cards out of Gronk’s meaty hands.

“I love messing with him,” Bradshaw will tell me. “He’s so dialed in. I try to un-dial him.”.

Industry observers note that A half-century ago, Bradshaw turned a country-bumpkin persona into a half-century career as a pitchman, musician, and NFL broadcaster. He recognizes a fellow traveler.

In a recent development, “The camera loves him,” indicates Bradshaw. “He’s harmless. It’s easy to like him.”.

It has been revealed that harmless is not the word I’d apply to a man who spent 11 NFL seasons beating the shit out of defenders, but Bradshaw has a point. Gronkowski’s secret power is that he conjures up Yogi Bear rather than Tony Soprano. No man eating Frosted Flakes out of a giant bowl in their man cave is going to worry that Gronk thinks he is smarter than them.

Television did not come naturally. Gronk understood football instinctually, seeing linebackers and safeties the way Jaws might size up a baby dolphin. Explaining what he saw in TV soundbites was another thing. During his first years at Fox, he prepared for TV as if he was the awkward lead in a high school play.

Looking back on his playing days, Gronk says, “I’m shocked I was able to do it all.”.

“I would remember a whole paragraph,” states Gronk. “I would say word for word the whole paragraph. It wasn’t fun being on TV like that.”.

Sources indicate that his producer, Bill Richards, could see Gronk laboring. Richards reminded him that the show was not a three-act play. He told him just to listen to the other men at the desk and then react to what they remarked.

Sources indicate that “This is live TV,” Richards told him. “We want you for what you think at the moment.”.

Sources indicate that richards bristles slightly when I wonder if Fox hired Gronk for comic relief, a Chris Farley type talking about the NFL’s best edge rushers. Sure, there are the stunts — Gronk once jumped from a military helicopter into the Pacific Ocean for the show, which led Strahan to observe that Gronk hasn’t “learned what to do is say no when asked to do stuff.” Still, Richards wants the audience to remember that Gronk the crash-test dummy was also one of the greatest football players ever.

“He’s not just the frat guy,” indicates Richards. “He knows football.”.

Recent findings suggest that being Gronk requires a willingness to look ridiculous. That’s A-OK for Gronk. In a segment that initially was filmed as an in-house joke, the Fox crew invented a Dallas Cowboys tight end and asked Gronk to analyze him, since he played the position. Gronk searched his memory for the name. Nothing. The player did not exist, but Gronk did not panic. He pivoted to the Cowboys’ actual tight end, Jake Ferguson, and explained how quarterback Dak Prescott would continue looking for him. The prank worked because Gronk was simultaneously dumb and smart. (Gronk loved the mischief, and the segment ran on the actual show.).

On set, Bradshaw needles him constantly. Gronk doesn’t mind; this is how ex-jocks express affection, through humiliation. Bradshaw clearly has great affection for Gronk. He worries about him like an agony aunt.

Recent findings suggest that “There was a time when I was the hottest young thing out there,” says Bradshaw. Now, Bradshaw watches Gronk go from show to ad shoot to the airport and back. “He’s gone, gone, gone,” says Bradshaw. “Commercial, commercial, commercial, all over the place.”.

Bradshaw warned Gronk to pace himself. At the Super Bowl in 2025, Gronk hit the wall.

“He was knocked out,” states Bradshaw. “He was so tired. He’d been going, going, going. For the Super Bowl, he must have had 88 events.”.

Recent findings suggest that gronk rejects the premise. He has brought professional discipline to the business of being Gronk. He sleeps, does hot yoga, does his ozone thing, and restores himself before the next encounter.

I ask Gronk if it gets exhausting being, well, Gronk for the masses.

“I can’t always be on, and I can’t satisfy everyone,” claims Gronk.

Recent findings suggest that this sounds like common sense until you understand Gronk’s predicament. His fans approach him and want good-guy Gronk who spikes footballs, makes 69 jokes, and invites them in ads for FanDuel to blow their paychecks and join the Sportsbook Reward Club. They don’t want to see a glowering Gronk wearing sunglasses in first class.

According to recent reports, edelman knows when his buddy hits his limit. An exhausted Gronk, he says, is like a dog whose owner has left him alone for three days. He is still Gronk, but the light has gone out of his eyes.

Sources indicate that gronkowski gives a dismissive wave when anyone suggests he works too much. He insists that he and his girlfriend, Camille Kostek, a former Patriots cheerleader, love to put their phones away and just chill at their New England home.

I don’t buy it. Work is both the cause of that exhaustion and the cure for something else. Football ended abruptly for Gronkowski, as it does for nearly everyone in the NFL. He first retired at 29, returned to win another Super Bowl with Brady in Tampa, and left for good at 33.

All his life, somebody told Gronk where to be and what to do. At Patriots training camp, his days began at seven in the morning and ended at 10 at night. Practices, meetings, treatments, meals, and film study swallowed every waking hour. He remembers that existence now with something close to wonder.

“I’m shocked how I was able to do it all.”.

But the absence of structure proved just as disorienting. After retirement, he would look at an empty week and initially feel liberated. Then he’d get restless.

Sources indicate that “I’m already bored,” Gronk remembers thinking. “What do I do with myself?”.

Football provided the structure that made the fun possible. Now, the business of being Gronk serves the same purpose. The difference today is there is no offseason.

It’s now around 5:45 p.m., and Gronk sheds his suit and heads to a decidedly less-flashy part of the Fox studio, one filled with Alexi Lalas memorabilia. Gronk and his friend Edelman prepare to tape their podcast, The Gronk & Jules Show. Both have been working for 12 hours. Now, they must reconstruct the day in football and push premium dog chow.

The podcast is where Gronk’s football intelligence and Gronk’s foolishness peacefully coexist. He explains how a strong running game pulls linebackers forward, opening the middle of the field for massive plays. But then he guesses that Saints quarterback Tyler Shough was drafted in the fifth, sixth, or seventh round. A producer informs him Shough was the 40th overall pick.

“Might as well be the sixth,” notes Gronk. “Might as well.”.

He is now babbling like a giant toddler who missed his afternoon nap, but it works. Gronk says an AI version of himself must have made one of his incorrect predictions. He theorizes that Elon Musk named Grok after him but removed the “n” to avoid paying for the naming rights.

Recent findings suggest that eventually, it is time for ad reads. One is for Carhartt. Gronk whispers to Edelman.

“I don’t even know what Carhartt is.”.

Edelman tells him it’s work clothes for men.

A minute later, Gronk is wearing a Carhartt sweatshirt, riffing about the protective qualities of the garment for Buffalo Bills fans diving on folding tables, as they like to do.

In a recent development, “You know you’re not going to break your arm,” states Gronk. “And if you do, it’s just not going to hurt as much.”.

Recent findings suggest that someone up the chain of command has decided that the ad reads should be preceded by some classic Edelman and Gronk banter. Today, that means a lengthy read for Sundays for Dogs devolves into a discussion of how dry dog food produces dry dog shit while wet dog food produces — you guessed it — wet dog shit.

Finally, the two are done. Gronk is out on his feet. Before he disappears into a waiting car, I ask him how tired he is.

It has been revealed that gronk begins explaining the advantages of recording the podcast immediately after the Fox show, when the games are still fresh in their minds. Then he stops.

And then he is gone. Gronk needs a nap.

Why a Mathematician Is Chasing Eclipses With Algorithms and Cameras

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3353 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With custom-built gear, his team seeks to solve a long-standing solar mystery.
  • Advanced image-processing software developed by Miloslav Druckmüller combines scores of individual images, captured during a total solar eclipse and painstakingly calibrated.
  • The sun hangs low over the plains of Castile and León, in the north-central region of Spain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With custom-built gear, his team seeks to solve a long-standing solar mystery.

Advanced image-processing software developed by Miloslav Druckmüller combines scores of individual images, captured during a total solar eclipse and painstakingly calibrated. The techniques reveal fine details in the sun’s corona, which is white in this image. The tiny pink shapes seen along portions of the edge of the blacked-out solar disk are prominences, which are extensions of relatively cool plasma that can jut out hundreds of thousands of kilometers into space.

The sun hangs low over the plains of Castile and León, in the north-central region of Spain. But from a slope of the mountain Pico Trigaza, it appears that a few puffy white clouds have started to block the sun. That’s vexing.

Sources indicate that A group of researchers, some wearing cardboard eclipse glasses, is clustered around sets of portable telescopes and cameras connected to laptops. All this gear is scattered on tabletops perched on the mountainside. On the computer screens, the sun’s disk looks like a deep orange crescent that is slowly waning. That’s because the moon began to crawl across it about half an hour ago. In 25 minutes, it will obscure the sun completely, producing an eerie and wondrous phenomenon—a total solar eclipse.

In a recent development, in the late-summer, late-afternoon heat, the researchers watch anxiously as those fluffy clouds linger around the sun. From an abandoned hut on the slope a few meters above, where the researchers have set up camp, one of the grad students emerges and nods toward the cloud formation. “Do you think it will dissolve?” he blurts out.

“It will.” Miloslav Druckmüller glances calmly at his group of doctoral candidates, now making final checks of the equipment in preparation for totality. Here in Spain, on this 12th day of August, Druckmüller is getting ready for his 19th solar eclipse. He knows from long experience that weather can turn quickly when the moon’s shadow suddenly pushes the temperature down. Plus, there’s no sense in riling up the grad students any more than they already are.

Miloslav Druckmüller led the design and construction of a unique optical instrument that incorporates eight astrocameras. Each is equipped with a spectral filter for sensing and recording specific emission spectra from the solar corona. Each of those spectra, in turn, is associated with a particular ionic species of iron atoms. Because the temperature needed to ionize iron varies depending on the ionic species, analyzing the locations and relative abundance of these ionic species offers valuable insights into the distribution of heat in the corona.Václav Široký.

In a recent development, during totality, the moon blocks the overwhelming glare of the solar disk, revealing delicate structures in the sun’s outer atmosphere, the corona. Using custom-built telescope systems and image-processing techniques that Druckmüller has spent decades developing, the researchers aim to gain insights into the processes in this enigmatic region that is otherwise hard to study. In addition to imaging the visible coronal light, the team will try to track the dispersal of superhot ions of iron into interplanetary space, which could give rare insights into the pattern of heat emanating from the corona.

And they’ll have 107 seconds to do all that.

It has been revealed that druckmüller is a professor of mathematics and image processing at the Brno University of Technology in the Czech Republic and a leading figure in the Solar Wind Sherpas, an international team that studies the sun’s corona during total eclipses. In the solar eclipse world, he is nothing short of a legend, albeit a reluctant one.

Recent findings suggest that an image from Miloslav Druckmüller’s first solar-eclipse expedition, to Hungary, vividly shows Baily’s Beads. These elongated white lights along a piece of the left edge of the blacked-out solar disk are caused by beams of sunlight shining through gaps in the irregular lunar surface during the eclipse. The pink shapes are solar prominences, which are jets of plasma extending out into space and held in place by the sun’s intense magnetic field.

He photographed his first solar eclipse in 1999, in what he thought would be a one-off lark. During that eclipse, the moon’s deep shadow missed Druckmüller’s native Czechia by just a few tens of kilometers, so he chased it to Hungary with a 30-year-old Soviet MTO 1,000-millimeter lens. All he remembers from that day is the rush of adrenaline he felt while trying to find the sun in the sky with the lens’s minuscule field of view and keep it in focus for the two minutes of the eclipse.

Industry observers note that he insists that he has never enjoyed any of the eclipses he has photographed. “In fact, I have never properly seen any of those eclipses. You are just watching the screens, making sure that it’s all doing what it’s supposed to do. There are so many things that can go wrong and you can’t redo it.”.

A composite sequence of photographs shows the 12 August 2026 solar eclipse as seen from a slope of the mountain Pico Trigaza in Spain.

Václav Široký and Miloslav Druckmüller.

In a recent development, despite Druckmüller’s outward tranquility on this Spanish hillside, the stakes are high. Just 45 minutes ago, his group heard from their colleagues in Iceland, where viewing conditions had promised to be better than in Spain. But a vast low-pressure system had clouded the entire sky, leaving all three Iceland teams without a view.

On the Pico Trigaza mountain in Spain, two postgraduate researchers used a laser to get a rough, initial alignment for the tracking mount of an optical instrument. The alignment was necessary to precisely compensate for the Earth’s motion.

The corona has been a mystery for centuries. Though dimmer—by a factor of a million—than the sun’s visible surface, the corona is nevertheless extremely hot: about a million degrees Celsius compared to 5,500 degrees on the surface. Because the sun’s nuclear fusion engine churns at the star’s heart, it might seem that temperatures should fall farther from the core.

Industry observers note that to observe the faint corona in visible light, researchers must block the sun’s ferocious glare. Specialized telescopes called coronagraphs do this with an opaque disk called an occulter. But because light bends around the occulter’s edges in an effect called diffraction, it must block an area much larger than that of the solar disk to prevent light from spilling over and ruining the images. But doing so means obstructing the inner part of the corona, which harbors the most key processes that underpin the puzzling phenomena of the sun’s upper atmosphere.

According to recent reports, that’s why total eclipses matter so much to solar physicists. By sheer chance, the moon is exactly the right size and at just the right distance to completely cover the sun during a total solar eclipse. Because the moon is so far away from Earth, the view is not marred by diffraction, and the corona reveals itself nearly all the way down to the sun’s surface.

As astrocameras recorded spectral data about the sun’s corona, a laptop computer [on table, at left] displayed the phase of the eclipse.

It has been revealed that space probes can image the solar surface in other wavelengths, but those views have limitations, too. Spacecraft such as NASA’s Solar Dynamics Observatory do see the innermost parts of the corona in extreme ultraviolet light, explains Shadia Habbal, a solar physicist at the University of Hawaii and leader of the Solar Wind Sherpas project. “But it cuts off very swiftly, so you don’t see its extension into space as well as we can see it in the visible emission lines” during an eclipse. “That’s the biggest advantage,” she says, of solar eclipse photography.

The European Proba-3 mission, debuted in 2024, simulates total solar eclipses by flying two spacecraft in a formation 150 meters apart with one acting as an occulter and the other as the telescope. The instruments aboard that satellite, however, have limitations compared to the equipment used by the Solar Wind Sherpas team.

When Druckmüller developed the film from his 1999 eclipse expedition, the photographs didn’t do justice to the event’s eerie beauty. He spent countless evenings applying his expertise in numerical image processing in an attempt to re-create in his photographs the sights he witnessed in that Hungarian corn field.

Sources indicate that it took two years, but eventually he succeeded. Where before there were dull views of the blackened lunar disk surrounded by the blunt wisps of the corona, Druckmüller revealed the subtlest details of the magnetic field lines stretching from the sun far into space. As his photographs circulated among solar physicists, invitations to eclipse expeditions began to arrive.

Solar researchers Miloslav Druckmüller and Shadia Habbal have been collaborating for two decades and 15 eclipses.

It has been revealed that habbal learned about the images from a Ph.D. student who had seen them at a conference presentation that didn’t credit Druckmüller. When Habbal’s team later published the images in a paper, they misattributed them to another researcher. Druckmüller found out through an astrophysicist friend. “I wrote her a rather disappointed email and she responded within 10 minutes,” Druckmüller recalls. “She really didn’t have a clue.”.

The error was corrected, and within weeks, Habbal and Druckmüller began a collaboration that grew into a friendship. “Milos’s processing brings out details that nobody has seen before, and they tell you a lot about very tiny features in the corona that you don’t see otherwise,” notes Habbal.

Capturing the corona’s delicate structures means finding a way to show its brightest and faintest features in the same image. “During the solar eclipse, the contrast between the darkest and brightest parts of the corona is enormous, possibly one to a million,” Druckmüller explains. “But a computer monitor only allows you to display a contrast ratio of one to about 800.” (Some modern monitors, particularly OLED ones, can deliver higher contrast ratios.).

Recent findings suggest that the human eye can adjust to this enormous range of brightness, allowing an observer to see both the bright corona and the faint stars and planets that briefly emerge in the darkened sky. To bring those details together in a photograph, Druckmüller uses custom image-processing algorithms to combine exposures that capture different parts of that range.

Researchers Martin Šebek and Peter Urgoš make fine adjustments to the focus and alignment of the astrocameras on a key optical instrument before the 12 August solar eclipse.

Industry observers note that to create a single image, Druckmüller’s teams need to take 200 individual frames during the eclipse at exposure times ranging from 0.001 second to two seconds. The data must then be calibrated against a vast number of reference images to filter out noise and imperfections. Flat fields, which depict a uniform light background, help correct for defects caused by telescope optics, dust spots, and variations in pixel sensitivity. Dark frames, taken with light blocked from the sensor, help correct for artifacts created by the camera’s image sensor itself. “It takes the computer more than two days to process one image,” Druckmüller says. Including the calibration data, a single finished image requires about 3,000 input frames.

Recent findings suggest that since 2008, teams directed by Habbal and Druckmüller have traveled to every total solar eclipse, spreading out across multiple locations to hedge against bad weather. About half of the teams return with usable data. For the others, it’s just a short and stressful voyage. For the 12 August eclipse, three groups deployed to Iceland and two to Spain.

It has been revealed that the teams seek sites close to the center of the band of totality, where the moon blocks the sun for longest. In Spain, the 12 August band of totality cut across the north of the country; the center line of the shadow passed within 11 kilometers of Pico Trigaza, promising Druckmüller and his colleagues a precious 107 seconds of totality.

But duration is only part of the calculation. Totality on Pico Trigaza will commence 51 minutes before sunset, with the sun just 8 degrees above the horizon. That low, the rays must pass through a much thicker layer of the atmosphere than when the sun is higher in the sky, increasing the light distortion that complicates photography. At the researchers’ camp on Pico Trigaza, 1,600 meters above sea level, the thinner air should help a bit.

An abandoned hut on the mountain Pico Trigaza in Spain was spruced up so that it could serve as a home base for the research team recording the 12 August solar eclipse.

Sources indicate that “Iceland would have been a much better place for us than Spain because the sun was higher up, some 25 degrees above the horizon,” Druckmüller says wistfully. But Iceland’s notoriously unpredictable weather made Spain an essential backup.

If you pack a van with thousands of dollars’ worth of cameras and optical gear and then set out on a 2,351-kilometer journey, you shouldn’t be surprised if you finish the trip with a few striking photographs [top]. The sleeping arrangements for the grad students at the Pico Trigaza hut [bottom] were spartan, but the views were first-rate.Top: Martin Šebek; Bottom: Václav Široký.

Recent findings suggest that on the mountain, locals have spruced up a rustic, long-unused hut for the researchers, running power cables from a nearby telecommunication outpost and bringing in a water tank. Five Ph.D. students drove more than 2,000 kilometers from Brno and have spent nearly a week preparing the equipment. Druckmüller and his wife joined them two days before the eclipse. They cook on a small propane grill and sleep in sleeping bags on yoga mats. “We have plenty of space here to set up our telescopes, beautiful views, and a roof over our heads,” Druckmüller says with a grin. “It’s perfect.”.

But even the best equipment and a carefully chosen site count for nothing if the clouds roll in. “So much work goes into the preparations and then, if you end up with nothing, you just feel terrible sadness,” indicates Jana Hoderová, an assistant professor of mathematics at Brno University of Technology and one of Druckmüller’s key collaborators.

Industry observers note that as the moon continues to slide in front of the solar disk, the pesky cumulus cloud that kept everybody on edge begins to dissolve. It’s 10 minutes to totality. The relief is palpable.

The countdown on the computers that control the cameras has begun. The screens are now showing only a tiny orange sliver, and the evening is becoming perceptibly less bright.

Recent findings suggest that twenty astrophotography cameras, most of them drawing power from a car battery that was also buffering the cameras from any grid instabilities, are pointed at the sun. Alongside equipment capturing the corona’s visible light, the team has built an assembly of eight cameras to detect light emitted by various iron ions that arise in the corona.

In a recent development, among the optical gear assembled at Pico Trigaza to capture the 12 August solar eclipse was a unique instrument designed to record the distributions of iron ions in the corona [at left]. Václav Široký.

Those instruments looking for iron ions have been put together with resourcefulness and thrift. A colleague of Druckmüller’s laser-cut the aluminum plates holding the carefully aligned lenses in exchange “for two bottles of whisky.” The brackets and attachments were 3D-printed at Brno University of Technology. The lenses, produced for the defunct camera maker Contax, were bought at steep discounts on eBay. By far the most expensive elements are interference filters that isolate the wavelengths emitted by the iron ions.

It has been revealed that around the blackened solar disk rises the magnificent golden halo of the corona. In the hush on the mountainside, it seems that even the birds have gone still.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s something nobody else in the world can do,” Druckmüller says with visible satisfaction. The unique technology, codeveloped with Habbal’s Hawaii team, has already enabled researchers to map the distribution of temperatures across the entire corona and to discover previously unseen structures, dubbed “smoke rings,” in the coronal plasma. The photographs also revealed the boundary region where the solar plasma becomes so thin that its ions stop colliding.

Recent findings suggest that the optical assembly designed to record the distributions of iron ions in the corona is outfitted with astrocameras, each of which captures spectra from a different ionic species. To do that, each astrocamera is equipped with a spectral filter whose bandwidth is so narrow—one nanometer—that the filter appears as a mirror.Martin Fornůsek.

“Iron is the most abundant of the heavy elements that we see in the solar corona,” notes Habbal. “And because the corona is so hot, the iron atoms lose electrons and get ionized. The larger the loss, the higher the temperature.”.

In a recent development, for example, a temperature of around 1.6 million °C is necessary to produce an iron ion that has lost 12 electrons. But only 1.4 million °C is needed to strip an iron atom of 11 electrons. Once it’s in a particular electrical state, the ion retains its specific ionization, even as it travels outward with the solar wind. Each of those ions, whether +11 or +12, emits a different wavelength of light, allowing the researchers to map not just temperatures within the corona, but also how those iron ions spread into interplanetary space and distribute heat. Habbal and her colleagues had long been trying to image those iron ions during solar eclipses. But it wasn’t until Druckmüller entered the picture that they were able to develop the gear and the mathematical techniques to do it.

According to recent reports, with just a minute to go to totality, the researchers begin removing protective filters from the lenses. It’s 50 minutes to sunset, and the waning sun has just begun to light up the clouds above the horizon with the first tinge of orange. Then, suddenly, the evening begins a rapid and premature descent into darkness. Along the edge of the fantastically thin solar crescent, the brilliant orange points known as Baily’s Beads flash and disappear—the last fragments of photospheric light visible through deep lunar valleys. As totality begins, observers remove their glasses. The hot air cools. The graduate students remain quietly and intently focused on their gear.

In a recent development, druckmüller looks up from his camera toward the darkened plains. Around the blackened solar disk rises the magnificent golden halo of the corona. In the hush on the mountainside, it seems that even the birds have gone still. The sky is ablaze with fiery colors all along the horizon where the deep lunar shadow drops off. Venus burns brilliantly in the southwest, a sharp white pinpoint in the darkened sky. The sound of camera shutters suddenly fills the air. Then, as quickly as it fell, the darkness begins to recede, bid farewell with another handful of golden Baily’s Beads.

According to recent reports, the crowd erupts in cheers. The Ph.D. students throw themselves at each other and hug like they mean it.

Sources indicate that “The students did most of the work this time, so I actually allowed myself to really look at it,” Druckmüller says. “It was beautiful. Pico Trigaza may not have been the best for science photography, but from the aesthetic point of view, it was extraordinary.”.

The 2026 solar-eclipse team at Pico Trigaza in Spain included [from left] Magdalena Šrotířová, Peter Urgoš, Martin Fornůsek, Miloslav Druckmüller, Václav Široký, and Martin Šebek.Václav Široký.

According to recent reports, but for Druckmüller, this is just the beginning. While other eclipse chasers will race to release their images, he will take his time. He expects to publish the first visible-light images of the corona in about two weeks. Processing the iron-ion images, and uncovering whatever insights they may hold, will take months—maybe even a whole year.

“Probably until the next eclipse in 2027” in North Africa, Druckmüller says.

Recent findings suggest that who knows? Maybe he’ll even enjoy that one, too.

iOS 27 brought fresh features to Apple Wallet, Maps, Notes, Messages, and more—and it includes key upgrades for the Mail app too. Here’s everything new for Apple Mail in iOS 27.

If you have much history using Apple Mail, you’ll know that its search feature hasn’t always been the best. But in iOS 27, search has gotten a massive upgrade.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Phil Barker, drummer for British punk rock band the Buzzcocks from 1992 through 2006, died on Nov. 21 at age 65 on the Isle of Wight, England. His death following a battle with an unspecified form of cancer was unveiled by the band on Nov. 26.

According to recent reports, “We’re saddened by the news of the passing of our longtime drummer Phil Barker,” the band wrote on their website. “He died peacefully in his sleep on Saturday, November 21, 2026 on the Isle of Wight, after a five-year battle with cancer. He is survived by Deb, his wife of 26 years.”.

Recent findings suggest that they continued, “Phil joined the band alongside bassist and childhood friend Tony Barber in 1992, backing Pete Shelley and Steve Diggle. He was integral to our success throughout that era, and left the band in early 2006. Just good memories. He will be missed.”.

Recent findings suggest that the Buzzcocks were founded in 1976 by Pete Shelley and Howard Devoto, who left the band sthe following year. The group released three albums before disbanding in 1981. They reformed in 1989 and released their fourth album, Trade Test Transmissions, in 1993. It was during this era that Barker joined the lineup as drummer alongside bassist Tony Barber. He collaborated on five albums with the group prior to Shelley’s death in 2018.

Recent findings suggest that diggle paid tribute to Barker on social media, writing, “I’m remembering the good times Phil and you were a great Drummer. Thinking of you Debbie and family. Tonight we play st Petersburg Florida and I will dedicate songs and the whole show to you Phil.” Trending Stories Duran Duran Guitarist Andy Taylor Dead at 65 Watch Miranda Lambert Perform Medley of Her Hits at Dallas Cowboys Halftime Show ⁠Gérard Depardieu to Face Trial for Allegedly Raping Actress Charlotte ⁠Arnould Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor Was the Wildest of the Wild Boys.

In a recent development, during his career, Barker also recorded with Slaughter Joe and The Modern Folk Quintet, occasionally working under the alias Phil Phuture. During the 1980s, he played with Lack of Knowledge. More recently, he performed with Crass vocalist Steve Ignorant in Stratford Mercenaries and punk band Dirt. The Buzzcocks have continued releasing music and touring since Shelley’s death. Barker left the group in 2006.

In a recent development, local record shop Triple A Records paid tribute to Barker on Facebook. “We’re very sad to hear our brilliant friend Philip Barker has passed away,” they wrote. “Phil drummed on our favourite Buzzcocks records and was a keen and generous supporter of the shop. We’ll be playing some of his music today as we think about his cheery visits. RIP mate x.”.

According to recent reports, back in July, PrismML claimed its roughly 4 GB, 1-bit Bonsai 27B was the first AI model of its size to run on an iPhone. Now PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an upgrade to the model it introduced in September.

The startup also drew attention when CEO Babak Hassibi told CNBC that Apple was evaluating its technology, as we reported at the time.

The new model is based on Qwen3.8 27B and keeps the same 5.9 GB footprint in its most compact format. This time, PrismML focused on helping the model handle longer tasks, including figuring out what to do when a tool returns an unexpected result or a step fails.

Bonsai 2.5 improved on six of the seven benchmarks PrismML highlights. Its SWE-bench Verified coding score rose from 60.8 to 75.6, while its AppWorld tool-use score jumped from 51.2 to 90.5. LiveCodeBench v6 dipped from 83.8 to 83.0.

Sources indicate that what could that look like on a Mac? A coding assistant could inspect a private project, make a change, run the tests, and use the results to revise its fix. A document app could summarize a folder of sensitive files while keeping the processing on the device.

PrismML says Bonsai 2.5 runs on Mac, iPhone, and iPad through MLX. Its Apple silicon package is about 8.9 GB, and the model card walks through setup on a Mac. The weights are available for free under Apache 2.0.

For a closer look at how the model was compressed and tested, read PrismML’s technical white paper.

#223197. Latest Update: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (2971 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2971 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

It has been revealed that the tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

Recent findings suggest that this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

According to recent reports, “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” notes Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Sources indicate that phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

Recent findings suggest that more than 10 years in the making, MMX introduced on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

Recent findings suggest that MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to strategy, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

In a recent development, once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to proposal, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

Sources indicate that during its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu states, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

In a recent development, idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

Industry observers note that “It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

It has been revealed that A simulation demonstrates how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” claims Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she claims. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

Sources indicate that the team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday states.

It has been revealed that despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday states Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

It has been revealed that idefix’s interactions with its upcoming home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec notes. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

According to recent reports, what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel claims the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Recent findings suggest that once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

In a recent development, the MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

It has been revealed that the pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this problem and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

Sources indicate that that possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

According to recent reports, during the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Recent findings suggest that once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

“MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu states. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

Latest Update: An annoying ‘mistake’ in macOS was actually prep for the latest MacBook Pro

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You may remember that Apple made a seeming mistake in the user interface for macOS 26, meaning that attempts to resize windows would often fail.
  • Industry observers note that I was one of a number of people to note that trying to grab the corner of a window in macOS Tahoe in order to resize it would often fail.
  • It turns out that my initial click in the window corner instinctively happens in an area where the window doesn’t respond to it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You may remember that Apple made a seeming mistake in the user interface for macOS 26, meaning that attempts to resize windows would often fail. The reason for this has now become clear, and Apple has done something both fun and clever in macOS 27 to resolve it ….

Industry observers note that I was one of a number of people to note that trying to grab the corner of a window in macOS Tahoe in order to resize it would often fail. Developer Norbert Heger pointed out this is because Apple changed the radius of the corners without changing the grabbable area.

It turns out that my initial click in the window corner instinctively happens in an area where the window doesn’t respond to it. The window expects this click to happen in an area of 19 × 19 pixels, located near the window corner. If the window had no rounded corners at all, 62% of that area would lie inside the window. But due to the huge corner radius in Tahoe, most of it – about 75% – now lies outside the window.

Industry observers note that at the time, the radius change itself looked like an inexplicable mistake on Apple’s part, and the firm did revert it. However, Macworld’s Michael Simon appears to have discovered the reason for the original change.

The new rounder corners on the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR are basically a perfect match for the macOS 26 radii.

Recent findings suggest that so if you move a window to the corner of the latest machine, it would fit perfectly. However, since Apple reverted the corner radius, it would no longer do so. The manufacturer solved this by a clever UI transition.

Recent findings suggest that what’s happening there is Golden Gate’s 20-point corner radius is subtly and gradually expanding when It approaches the bottom corner of the screen to match the exact corner of the display, which is much larger. I can’t be certain it’s exactly 26-point, but it sure looks like it to me. The effect is incredible. I’ve watched it like 20 times and I can barely see it changing, yet when it reaches the corner it’s perfectly expanded to match.

You can see this illustrated by a GIF in the Macworld piece. While the original change annoyed me, Apple’s solution is the perfect example of the manufacturer sweating the details.

💡 Key Takeaways

As autonomous AI agents work together, verifying their actions, enforcing security policies, and maintaining accountability becomes increasingly difficult.

Vishal Sharma is a Reader in the School of Electronics, Electrical Engineering, and Computer Science at Queen's University Belfast, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom.

In a de-authentication attack on an aerial vehicle using a human- and agent-in-the-loop approach, an AI agent can quickly scan the active channel and autonomously intercept traffic, thus reducing the time to react and regain control.

Sources indicate that QLED. OLED. Mini-LED. The TV world can be super overwhelming, so let’s do a quick rundown of the differences between the three “premium” panel types.

According to recent reports, OLED TVs have lots of mini diodes inside the panel that emit light individually. This means there’s no backlight, unlike older TVs. As a result, OLEDs are better for higher contrast, better blacks, better color, and smooth motion for gaming.

In a recent development, QLEDs also use a light-emitting diode. Unlike OLED, a QLED panel has a backlight, which illuminates each diode individually. QLEDs are better for brighter rooms, as the panel itself tends to be brighter, but OLEDs can reach better contrast levels and color accuracy.

Recent findings suggest that mini-LED is something else entirely: it uses tiny LEDs (light-emitting diodes, like both QLED and OLED) — but thousands of them. That means each diode can pack a major color and brightness punch. Mini-LEDs can be brighter, blacker, and more colorful — all at once.
