  • Microsoft has explained more about why it took so long to resolve the concern and said that it’s urgently working on newly introduced approaches to resolve any future incidents in less than an hour ….
  • Code Red is a common term used to describe the highest priority response to a major problem, pulling a significant number of engineers off their current tasks in order to maximize the resources applied to fixing it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The recent Microsoft 365 outage was the worst the service had ever experienced, with more than 80% of the company’s servers unresponsive at the worst point. The company has now declared a Code Red to address the way it prevents and responds to major failures in future.

Microsoft has explained more about why it took so long to resolve the concern and said that it’s urgently working on newly introduced approaches to resolve any future incidents in less than an hour ….

Code Red is a common term used to describe the highest priority response to a major problem, pulling a significant number of engineers off their current tasks in order to maximize the resources applied to fixing it.

“Scattered across fragmented internal systems.” 😆.

As someone who works in IT and manages Microsoft products, I thought that was their entire design philosophy.

The senior execs responsible for the service told staff that it was the most customer-impacting incident ever experienced, and has acknowledged that not only was the problem itself unacceptable, but so too was the time taken to resolve it. Reuters got sight of a memo sent to the team.

It was the most ⁠customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online, M365 Core President Jason Henderson noted in a memo to staff on Friday. Never before had so many customers been without email for so long, he said. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson added.

Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures,” according to Silver’s memo.

One reason it took so long to work out what had happened was because the diagnostic data needed was “scattered across fragmented internal systems.” The memo indicates 11 separate Teams chats exchanged more than 11,000 messages as they struggled to work out what exactly had gone wrong.

Microsoft is now working on five interrelated approaches to achieve a target resolution time of less than an hour for any future incidents of this nature.

What's more, retailers are giving the iPad A16 a $50 discount ahead of Black Friday, bringing the entry-level price down to $399.

The iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro). It doesn't have the best display, the best camera, or the best processor. But it doesn't need those things: This iPad has a display, camera, and processor that are good enough for most use cases, without unnecessarily driving up the price. Simply put, it's one of the best tablets you can buy right now.

According to recent reports, the iPad A16 has a large, 11-inch (technically 10.86 inches, according to Apple's fine print) IPS display with a brightness of 500 nits. As the name implies, it has Apple's A16 chip, the same processor as the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 15. That chip is about four years old at this point, and while that means it won't be as fast as Apple's newer SoCs, it still holds its own with iOS 27. It comes with two cameras: One 12MP wide camera on the back, with support for 4K video recording, and a 12MP Center Stage camera on the front.

Apple says this iPad can run for 10 hours while browsing the internet on wifi or watching video. You charge the tablet with USB-C, which supports data transfer up to USB 2.0 (which nets you 480Mb/s transfer speeds). It also comes with other perks you might expect from Apple's more "pro" tablets. You can connect the iPad to an external display, up to 4K resolution at 60Hz. It also supports two Apple Pencil models: The USB-C Apple Pencil and the first-gen Apple Pencil.

It has been revealed that the only real consideration here is storage: This model comes with 128GB of storage, which can run out fast. It's particularly usable for people who rely on cloud storage or mostly stream their entertainment. But if your giftee aims to store photos, videos, or music on their iPad, it's worth considering upgrading. The $50 discount applies to most storage models, as well as the cellular iPad options, except for the 512GB models: The wifi-only model has a smaller discount, while the cellular option has a $100 discount.

Sure, the iPad A16 doesn't have the fastest processor, an OLED display, support for newer accessories, or Apple's sharpest cameras. But all of the specs it does have are enough to run the things you need on iPadOS. If someone on your list is looking for an iPad for web browsing, streaming, messaging, and light gaming—and they don't need something for professional work—this device is likely more than enough iPad for them.

Kate Middleton shared footage from her upcoming documentary, Heal, which sheds light on how she dealt with her cancer diagnosis.

Sources indicate that in the clip, shared on the Prince and Princess of Wales’ Instagram account on Friday, the royal says in a voiceover, “Navigating cancer or any longterm illness is a lonely road. But it’s clear we’re not carry life’s challenges alone. My illness has brought me alongside so many others navigating their own journeys too. This has become so much more than a personal or solitary experience, but really a collective one.”.

Middleton can then be seen joining a cancer support group, Shine Cancer Support. “Genuinely, meeting you all here today really means a lot to me because it’s just lovely to be able to share my personal experience, but also hear your stories and be able to connect with others who’ve gone through something similar,” she tells her fellow group members.

She adds, “I haven’t really explored this outside my family walls, really. So thank you for allowing me the time to do that and the open space to explore that. I really appreciate it, so thank you.”.

According to recent reports, heal: A Princess of Wales Story will air Nov. 30 on NBC, a day after it premieres on the BBC. The documentary follows Middleton as she reflects on her cancer battle while completing the Three Peaks Challenge — climbing the tallest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in the span of 24 hours — this past June in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, the hospital where she was treated; proceeds from the distribution of Heal will also benefit Royal Marsden.

The news of Middleton’s initial diagnosis was disclosed to the public in March 2024, following an abdominal surgery in January. In a video statement, Middleton stated, “At the time, it was thought that my condition was non-cancerous,” referring to her surgery. “The surgery was successful, however, tests after the operation on cancer had been present,” she added. Sources indicate that electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then shows how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

WhatsApp is developing a fresh format to add an audio track to a sticker. This would allow people to send a sticker that plays a sound when the recipient taps it.

You can create your own audio stickers by selecting one of your videos.

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (871 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the pulsing red world of the Upside Down in Stranger Things, rocks and debris fly as Max runs for her life to the soundtrack of Kate Bush’s “Running Up That Hill (A Deal With God).” Wednesday Addams, dead serious in a to-die-for dress, does a wacky dance to the Cramps’ “Goo Goo Muck.” Today, television is one of music’s most powerful discovery platforms, introducing upcoming generations to older songs and giving familiar ones entirely new lives — but few series have wielded that influence as consistently or as commercially as Glee.

It has been revealed that at its height in March 2011, music from Glee occupied six of the Top 10 spots on iTunes’ Top Songs chart. The previous month, songs from Glee amassed 880,000 downloads. The show had been driving its viewers’ music consumption since it debuted in 2009, beginning with Journey’s 1981 classic “Don’t Stop Believin’,” the first Glee cast recording to reach the Billboard Hot 100 Top 10. Over its six-season run, the Glee cast scored 207 entries on the Hot 100, setting a chart record that surpassed the Beatles and Elvis Presley.

Recent findings suggest that glee brought songs by Queen, Barbra Streisand, and Michael Jackson back into the zeitgeist while reimagining hits of the day by Katy Perry and Adele. These fresh takes, coupled with the series’ candy-colored visuals and relatable characters, made for destination viewing — and listening.

Recent findings suggest that “One of the biggest reasons soundtracks are successful is because the consumer wants to relive the film or television experience,” notes PJ Bloom, who was Glee’s music supervisor. “We were creating seven to 10 singles with full-blown music videos each episode. We wanted them to be available to the consumer pretty much as soon as the show ended.”.

The timing for Glee’s singles-only weekly release schedule was ideal. Apple’s iTunes, introduced in 2001, was already an established music-purchasing platform. YouTube was still in its infancy, and Spotify wouldn’t arrive in the U.S. until 2011, taking some time to gain traction. Bypassing the manufacturing and distribution costs of physical product helped boost the bottom line. But after the show’s astronomical success, physical albums followed, with 14 reaching the Top 10 of the Billboard 200, including three consecutive Number Ones, and cumulative U.S. sales of more than 8 million. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

It wasn’t just the Glee cast versions that sold; the original recordings did, too. Had brick-and-mortar stores been the only option, it’s unlikely they would have stocked cassingles of long-out-of-print songs like Bon Jovi’s “It’s My Life” (2000) or Katrina and the Waves’ “Walking on Sunshine” (1983), both featured in the Oct. 7, 2009, Season One episode, “Vitamin D” — but they were just a click away on iTunes.

In a recent development, geoff Bywater, Fox’s head of music during Glee’s run, spent time working in the U.K., where he saw firsthand the impact that the weekly chart show Top of the Pops had on viewers. “It was an institution,” he claims. “Everybody in the family would gather around the TV to watch Top of the Pops. When I came back to this country and I was handed the script to Glee, I knew it was going to be massive because I had seen what culturally could happen around a family-oriented music show.”.

Within months of Glee’s premiere, The Hollywood Reporter published a story about how the series was “reviving a beleaguered music industry.” Leonard Richardson, then vice president of music at the CW, was quoted as saying, “TV has basically become the new radio. It is about exposure and making an impression.” (That observation is especially striking given radio’s resistance to playing Glee cast versions, no matter how popular they were.).

In a recent development, the “Glee Effect” translated to an uptick in school choirs and vocal groups after the series’ first season. And even in an age when TikTok plays a large part in how young audiences discover current music and songs from decades past, Glee is still doing its thing. The series has been available on streaming services since 2011. With a reboot now confirmed through Disney+ and Hulu, a new generation of students is catching up on the original seasons and recognizing the Glee cast renditions of the songs. Trending Stories Duran Duran Guitarist Andy Taylor Dead at 65 Watch Miranda Lambert Perform Medley of Her Hits at Dallas Cowboys Halftime Show ⁠Gérard Depardieu to Face Trial for Allegedly Raping Actress Charlotte ⁠Arnould Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor Was the Wildest of the Wild Boys.

“As much as Glee was about music, it really resonated with the American family and with families throughout the world,” indicates Bywater. “There were things in that show that culturally hit buttons, and those were buttons that were not easy to hit.”.

Sources indicate that “The world is littered with failed television musicals,” Bloom adds. “When we were doing the pilot, we all knew we were onto something special. But you can never predict the global-phenomenon effect Glee had.”.

In a recent development, nothing's first over-ear headphones, the Headphone (1), is $130 off for Black Friday, bringing them down to $169 from $299 (their lowest price ever). Nothing's newer Headphone (a), which debuted in 2026 and earned an "excellent" rating in PCMag's review, is on sale as well, dropping to $109 from $199. For more discounts and the latest offers, check out our extensive Black Friday 2026 coverage.

In line with the company’s design language, these headphones feature transparent elements and bold, geometric detailing that make them stand out from typical matte-black pairs. But the appeal goes beyond the look. These IP52-rated headphones use 40mm drivers, hybrid ANC, and both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. They also support high-res audio via LDAC, while Nothing’s companion app gives you basic and advanced EQ controls for adjusting the sound. Battery life is impressive, too, stretching to 35 hours with ANC on and up to 80 hours with it switched off.

It has been revealed that but the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

That remarked, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, with iPads running the same chips as Macs, many have wished Apple would give us the option of running macOS on them instead of the somewhat clunky iPadOS windowing system. Apple’s previous arguments against converging devices have been somewhat weakened by the launch of the touchscreen MacBook Pro.

A new report indicates that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either ….

According to recent reports, as iPad hardware has grown more powerful over the years, the software has struggled to keep up. We saw split-screen capabilities first, with full windowing finally coming to the devices in iPadOS 26 last year.

The UI is still rather clunky compared to macOS, however, leading a significant number of people to wish that Apple simply offered the option of using the more powerful operating system on its tablet devices.

I would be comfortable with 11" and 13" devices running macOS. Actually, I don’t require them to run macOS itself, but I do need them to run macOS apps. I wish the iPad could match a MacBook’s productivity. Running macOS on an iPad seems like a reasonable idea. The MacBook Air is now the better price choice, while those needing a powerhouse will always choose a MacBook Pro or Studio.

Some suggest that running macOS on iPad would reduce Mac sales, but I disagree. I own a nearly full-spec MacBook Pro 16" and expect to keep a machine like that, yet I also purchased a MacBook Air for lighter travel. I would prefer an iPad over the Air, but I cannot choose it because it lacks the apps I require. If it supported them, I would buy the iPad Pro with all accessories, and Apple would gain more revenue from me. I appreciate the concept of owning an iPad, but at the moment it lacks the value needed to justify paying more for a device that simply does less than a MacBook Air.

In a podcast Q&A, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman claims that Apple is already doing this internally, but there’s no sign of any plans to make it available outside the manufacturer.

Apple has iPads internally running macOS, and they’ve had that for some time. The fact that they have the underlying architecture of Apple Silicon that’s the same on the iPad and the Mac gives them the flexibility in order to test these types of things.

In a recent development, in terms if they’re actually going to do it – would they bring macOS to the iPad itself – at this point I don’t think that’s going to happen anytime soon. I’ve checked into this and there’s no ongoing operating system project right now in terms of a brand new operating system for the iPad – there is no work being done to consumerize macOs on the iPad.

Gurman says Apple seems set to continue to make piecemeal changes over time to bring iPad capabilities closer to those of the Mac but is showing no signs of full convergence.

He reiterated that work on a long-rumored giant-sized folding iPad continues.

The other thing I want to say is that I’m really excited for this potential of Project J312. That is, this giant 19-inch, 20-inch foldable iPad. And it’s basically like a gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside.

Sources indicate that however, he states there’s no guarantee it will ever launch, saying the timings have already slipped from 2027 through 2028 to 2029, but both cost and yield issues may still kill the project. If it does launch, it’s expected to cost anywhere from $3,000 to $5,000.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Rust library for building communications applications. SIP, RTP, WebRTC, QUIC/WebTransport/WebSocket conversations, Media over QUIC, and voice-AI agents share one call model, and the whole stack is in the box: no external SIP server, media server, or RTP engine to install and wire together.

Sources indicate that five-minute start · For carriers · Which crate? · Pick a path · How it fits together · What ships · Interop evidence · Changes · Upgrading from 0.3.

Industry observers note that rvoip is a library, not a server you deploy next to your application. Signalling, media, codecs, NAT traversal, security, and the conversation model are all Rust crates in this workspace, so a call goes from your code to the wire without a separately installed SIP proxy, media server, or RTP engine. The examples below run on a laptop with nothing installed but Rust; the same crates carry the release-gated interoperability evidence against Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, Jambonz, Kamailio, and OpenSIPS. Carriers evaluating standards coverage, performance, and reliability should start with For carriers.

From here, examples/ walks forward one step at a time: real microphone audio, registering to a PBX, hold/DTMF, transfers, SRTP and TLS, an IVR, a B2BUA, then browser and voice-AI gateways.

It has been revealed that the workspace contains 47 crates. You import one of them; it pulls in everything it needs. The rest are internal layers you never name in your own Cargo.toml.

According to recent reports, deployment backends (Keycloak, LDAP, Redis, Postgres vCon storage, audit and SIEM sinks, SAML, SCIM, WebAuthn, STIR/SHAKEN, IMS AKA) are separate rvoip-* extension crates you add only when you operate that backend. The extension catalog lists them.

According to recent reports, for JavaScript UCTP control, see the experimental browser/Node WebSocket client. It is available as source with TypeScript declarations; the package is not yet published to npm. Application-profile dispatch is a separate opt-in server extension that stock servers do not enable.

RvoipApp declares transports, roles, and routing through one builder and runs SIP, WebRTC, and UCTP listeners on the shared Orchestrator:.

Your SIP or WebRTC caller is bridged to the agent through the Orchestrator; the agent joins as its own AI participant with typed events, control messages, and supervised teardown. According to recent reports, every transport turns into the same objects, so an application written against the conversation model does not care whether a leg arrived over SIP, a browser, or QUIC. That is what lets one Orchestrator bridge them.

If you’ve been counting down to Black Friday and hoping for a deal on an Apple Watch, there’s no time like the present: Walmart recently launched its early Black Friday tech deals, and the rarely discounted Apple Watch Series 11 is right now $100 off, bringing the 42mm GPS model down to $299 (originally $399). The 46mm GPS model is $329 (originally $429), while the GPS + Cellular versions start at $399 and are also $100 off.

Though it has been supplanted by the Series 12, released earlier this fall, the Series 11 is still a great buy. It lasts up to 24 hours, making it a great option for everyday use and sleep tracking, and a 15-minute charge provides around eight hours of use. It has a strong selection of health features, including wrist temperature sensing, sleep score, ECG, heart-rate monitoring, and hypertension notifications, as well as detailed workout tracking. Compared with the Series 10, this aluminum model’s Ion-X display is twice as scratch-resistant. It’s also water-resistant to 50 meters.

While it doesn’t have the Series 12’s new processor or updated health-tracking features, the Apple Watch Series 11 is a great pick for your first Apple Watch or as an upgrade from an older model, such as the Series 8. Its large display, durability, and versatile staple features deliver the core Apple Watch experience at a more affordable price, especially if you don’t want Apple’s latest Audio Intelligence features.

In a recent development, iOS 27.3 includes many upcoming features for Apple’s built-in apps, but it also introduces design changes on the iPhone across Calendar, Safari, Music, and more. Here’s what’s new.

Recent findings suggest that apple is always iterating on the design of its software. While major overhauls like iOS 26’s Liquid Glass don’t come along often, the organization makes smaller design changes all the time via software updates. In iOS 27.3, which will launch to all users next month, Apple has design changes coming to four popular apps: Health, Calendar, Safari, and Music.

The Health app gets the biggest design changes.

As seen above, Health introduces brand upcoming Insights, Longevity, and Browse tabs that replace the previous options and include a variety of fresh UI elements like a top navigation row, personalized prompts and coaching, educational videos, and a lot more.

As the side-by-side above shows, the buttons for search and creating a new event have moved out of the top-right corner and into the bottom of the screen.

Calendar also now reveals the year at the top of the screen next to the current month, and has updated the ‘Today’ button to show the current date instead.

Safari introduces an optional fresh design for tabs: Vertical Tabs. You can enable these inside Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ Safari for a different approach to tabs across iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Here’s an example of vertical tabs on iPhone Duo.

Vertical Tabs won’t be for everyone, but they’ve proven popular in other browsers, so it’s great to see Safari add the option.

Recent findings suggest that song artwork is now able to break the constraints of a square and blend seamlessly into the scrolling lyrics view. Here are examples from Beta Profiles on X:.

Industry observers note that fresh in iOS 27.3 Beta: Animated artwork blends into the Apple Music player in landscape mode, and it looks so good. pic.twitter.com/k8rgSEALGo.

This lyrics view was previously available on iPhone Duo, but now it’s coming to all iPhones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that vim was too complicated. It wasn't worth the effort to learn it. Or so I thought.

I could write and edit my content after a couple of hours. Why everybody thought it was so hard?

Even better: I was more productive, I could focus solely on what I was writing, and I had so much fun!

Industry observers note that the fun never stopped. Even after playing with Vim for almost a decade.

A step-by-step approach to learn easily without feeling overwhelmed.

Practice makes perfect: no less than 170 fun exercises to build your muscle memory.

How to customize your editor for your own specific needs.

Keeping your hands on your keyboard will save your cognitive energy, and improve your productivity.

Hi! I'm Matthieu. Nice to see you here!

I've been coding as a hobby for 25 years, professionally for 15+ years.

I've worked from small to massive companies, mentoring and leading developer teams.

It has been revealed that teaching is very rewarding to me. That's why I love writing for my blog, The Valuable Dev.

Despite its reputation, Vim is not hard to learn. It works differently than most editor or IDE out there, that's why many people find it difficult. If you accept that it requires some adaptation, you can learn the basics in a couple of hours.

Vim is a good example of a tool easy to learn but hard to master: you'll add upcoming functionalities to your workflow overtime, improving your editing experience and your efficiency.

That's why this book takes a step-by-step approach.

This book is exclusively about Vim and Neovim running in a *nix shell (Unix-like shell like Zsh or Bash). This book is not about Vim running in a GUI, like GVim for example.

A price drop always stands out more when the product in question already has a reputation for delivering above its size, and that’s the case with the Bose SoundLink Plus. It hasn’t been on the market for long, but it’s already earned strong reviews—CNET labeled it “the Goldilocks of Bose Bluetooth speakers.” And right now, for Black Friday, it’s down to $179, which is the lowest price we've seen.

It has been revealed that bose positions it right in the middle of the SoundLink lineup, and you feel that balance in how it’s built. It’s compact enough to clip onto a backpack using its built-in nylon strap, and tough enough to handle getting knocked around, and sealed against dust and full water submersion with an IP67 rating. Battery life can last up to 20 hours, depending on the volume, which is sufficient for full-day outings. On the connectivity side, there’s Bluetooth 5.4 with AAC and AptX Adaptive support, as well as the ability to keep two devices paired for smoother switching. What you don’t get is a microphone, an aux port, or any voice assistant support, which is worth considering if you prefer wired options or use speakers for calls.

Recent findings suggest that as for its sound profile, it leans into mid- and high-bass, which gives electronic and pop tracks a lively pulse, though at higher volumes, you may notice some compression (which is common in speakers this size). It also doesn’t reach into true low-bass territory, so anyone who wants thumping sub-bass may not get it here, but the punch it does deliver feels clean for its size, notes this PCMag review. And while you won't get the width and separation of a stereo mix since the SoundLink Plus plays audio in mono, its directivity is good—meaning its sound remains clear from different listening positions, so you don't have to sit directly in front of it to get a good experience.

Sources indicate that as the gods and demigods of Percy Jackson and the Olympians return for Season 3, Courtney B. Vance had a mighty toga to fill.

The Golden Globe nominee, who returns after taking over the role of Zeus from the late Lance Reddick, remembered the actor as “a great, great man” before Reddick’s death at age 60 in March 2023.

“His stamp on this role is very strong, so I’m taking my time and making sure that I’m doing right by him,” he told People. “And by doing right by him, I do right by myself.” Watch on Deadline.

Vance added, “You have to do things right. Start the way you want to finish. I’m stepping into a very well-established family, so I want to make sure that I’m doing the right thing by them and myself. It was a little challenging at first, but they were very welcoming to me, so I’m grateful.”.

Shortly after wrapping on Season 1 of Percy Jackson, Reddick died at age 60 on March 17, 2023. Although a coroner ruled his cause of death to be heart disease, Reddick’s family disputed that report as inconsistent with his habits and fitness.

Although the show was initially hesitant to re-cast the character, Vance filled the role in late 2024, debuting in January’s Season 2 finale episode “The Fleece Works Its Magic Too Well.”.

With latest episodes available to stream Fridays on Disney+, Season 3 of Percy Jackson and the Olympians marks the first time The Titan’s Curse, the third book from Rick Riordan’s bestselling series, has been adapted for the screen.

It has been revealed that if Percy Jackson (Walker Scobell) learned anything after completing two epic quests with Annabeth Chase (Leah Sava Jeffries), it’s that he would be lost without her. So when Annabeth is captured by the forces of Kronos, Percy must embark on a perilous journey to rescue her. He must free a goddess in chains, confront the Titan’s curse, and avoid triggering the fall of Olympus. With Grover (Aryan Simhadri) by his side, Percy must join some unlikely questmates to confront a prophecy with dire consequences.

The day itself is here and the Black Friday deals are going strong. And this is one of my favorites. Right now, the brand-spanking-new Beats 360 — only released two months ago — are $100 off at Walmart.

According to recent reports, I'm Pete, reviews editor here at Tom's Guide. My team of expert reviewers and I test a heck of a lot of headphones. It's not often we see waterproofed over ears — unlike earbuds, waterproofing full headphones isn't an easy thing to do.

The Beats 360 are IPX4-rated, which means they're fully water- and sweatproofed, making these, in my opinion, the absolute best headphones for gym-goers.

Sources indicate that with IPX4 water- and sweatproofing, plus replaceable earcup and headband pads, the Beats 360 are the ultimate over ear headphones for working out. Despite only being released a couple of months ago, they're already $100 at Walmart.

We gave these headphones four stars in our Beats 360 review, and I get why. Although I didn't review them personally, I actually had my own set for around a month, so I took them for a spin.

It has been revealed that I was genuinely surprised by how good these cans sounded. I've seen reports online of the drivers making a hissing noise due to a QC problem, but I didn't experience that at all. The sound was fairly spacious for over ears, with that trademark Beats bass boost. As an iPhone user, I also appreciated that (as an Apple product) the Beats 360 offer that AirPods-esque Apple ecosystem experience. You control the headphones via settings rather than an app, and your connection switches devices with you.

In a recent development, best of all, though, I loved how these headphones performed for their primary intended purpose: working out. You can swap the ear and headband cushions, which is great for customizing them to your liking. My test set came with a set of comfy plush pads, but I chose to stick with the default breathable pads for working out. The best benefit of replacement pads though, is that if they get gross from sweat, you can swap them out.

The Beats 360 are also IPX4 rated. This means they have no dust or sand protection, but are fully water and sweat-resistant. This is rare on headphones, which are notoriously difficult to waterproof. The only other headphones we've tested recently with IP ratings are the Nothing Headphone (a), which are only IP52 (so better dustproofed but less water resistant) and the Bang & Olufsen Beoplay H95... which cost like $1,200.

Our running expert Nick Harris-Fry also took the Beats 360 on a 10-mile run, summing up his experience with: "If you love over-ear headphones, these are the best for running I’ve tried." So this deal is definitely one for all the fitness fanatics out there.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that gerald R. Molen, an Academy Award-winning producer behind Steven Spielberg‘s Amblin Entertainment, has died. He was 91.

On Sunday, Molen’s niece Rachel Pullan announced that he died earlier that day. “This morning my great uncle, Gerald R. Molen, passed on to join my great grandma and his dear wife Pat on the other side of the veil,” she wrote on Instagram. “I am so happy for him, and also so very sad.

“Uncle Jerry was a man of great moral character and high integrity. He started doing work, moving set pieces and driving at a movie studio, and worked his way up to the position of producer. He worked on many great films, including Jurassic Park, Schindler’s List (for which he won the Oscar for best production), Rain Man, Minority Report and The Other Side of Heaven, just to name a few. He held to his beliefs and standards and industry where that was often difficult to do. Minority Report is rated PG-13 because Jerry told Steven Spielberg he would only do the movie if it wasn’t rated R, and Spielberg made it happen—it was worth it to him to have Jerry be his producer. Jerry influenced millions of people, both by his example and his contributions to the telling of brilliant stories in film.” Related Stories Casting Steven Spielberg Sets Adaptation Of 'The Heart In Winter' As Next Film At Focus With Jessie Buckley, Cillian Murphy And Mark Rylance Starring And Paul Thomas Anderson Adapting The Script News In New Book, Joe Biden's National Security Aide Brett McGurk Describes Jeffrey Katzenberg & Steven Spielberg Advising POTUS On Major Gaza Speech.

It has been revealed that pullan added, “I’m glad I was able to go see Uncle Jerry a couple of times in the last few years before he passed. I will be watching Jurassic Park in his honor tonight. It was definitely one of his personal favorites stash as evidenced by the number of dinosaur she had on every surface in his house. Love you, Uncle Jerry— say hi to great Grandma for me.” Watch on Deadline.

Sources indicate that born Jan. 6, 1935 in Great Falls, Montana, Gerald Robert Molen grew up in North Hollywood after his family relocated there.

In 1985, Molen began working with Spielberg as a unit production manager on The Color Purple, before going on to produce his movies Hook (1991), Jurassic Park (1993) and Schindler’s List (1993), which earned them the Best Picture Oscar. They also worked together on The Lost World: Jurassic Park (1997), Amistad (1997), Minority Report (2002) and Catch Me If You Can (2002).

According to recent reports, amazon has cut prices across its entire Fire TV Soundbar lineup for Black Friday, with discounts covering everything from a basic two-channel soundbar designed to improve on your TV's built-in speakers to a full 5.1-channel setup with a wireless subwoofer and rear surround speakers. For more on the sale, you can also check out our Black Friday deals page, where we're covering the latest discounts ahead of this year's event.

Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is $74.99 (was $119.99), making it the least expensive option in the lineup for anyone who wants a step up from TV speakers for everyday viewing—it's a 24-inch, two-channel bar that supports DTS Virtual:X and Dolby Audio, though it doesn’t have Dolby Atmos or a separate subwoofer. Despite its name, it's an audio-only soundbar and requires a Fire TV streaming stick for you to get any of the Fire TV experience. For more on this soundbar, read PCMag’s review.

Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus is down to $139.99 from $249.99, and the extra money over the base model gets you a dedicated center channel that helps make dialogue easier to follow, along with a built-in subwoofer, Dolby Atmos, and DTS:X support. That said, it doesn’t have up-firing drivers, so the Atmos effect stays largely horizontal, but the center channel does real work on mumbled dialogue in prestige dramas. As with the base model, this one also handles audio only and needs a Fire TV device for any of the streaming features. This PCMag review has more detail on how it performs.

Industry observers note that amazon Fire TV Soundbar with Alexa Voice Remote Pro is $109.98 (was $154.98). This pairs the entry-level bar with the upgraded remote, which adds backlit buttons, two customizable shortcuts you can set for favorite apps or Alexa commands, and a remote finder (for when it inevitably disappears into the couch). If you don’t specifically want or need the remote, though, the Soundbar Plus is a more capable soundbar for just $30 more.

In a recent development, amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer is $229.99, down from $374.99. This configuration takes the same 3.1-channel bar and pairs it with a separate wireless subwoofer, which gives bass-heavy scenes and film scores considerably more weight than the bar's built-in woofer can manage on its own—and at $90 more than the discounted Soundbar Plus, this is the option I'd consider if fuller bass is a priority. Keep in mind that it doesn't add rear speakers, so you're still working with a 3.1 setup and sound that stays in front of you.

In a recent development, amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer and Surround Sound Speakers is $349.99, down from $489.99. This is the complete 5.1 package, adding two rear speakers to the 3.1 bar and wireless subwoofer, so action scenes and other surround effects come from behind you, rather than only from the direction of the TV—but it costs $120 more than the discounted soundbar and subwoofer bundle, so it’s worth considering how much you want that surround-sound effect. Also, while the rear speakers connect to the soundbar wirelessly, each still needs a power outlet.

Sources indicate that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've been using the XGIMI MoGo 3 Pro since it came out in 2024 and have been recommending it to friends and family every chance I get. It quickly became my favorite portable projector, and two years later, it's still my go-to for a spontaneous projector session. If you're on the lookout for a good deal on a portable projector, I recommend considering the following XGIMI deals.

In a recent development, if you're looking for the most affordable option, the Vibe One projector is just $179 (originally $299) after a 40% discount. This is a 1080p resolution and 1500:1 contrast portable projector for casual watching at night with 250 ISO lumens of brightness, and the price reflects that. It already comes with Google TV, which is my favorite OS, so you can download and stream any app you want. It's battery-powered, which means you can take it anywhere with you (as long as you have wifi). The battery lasts up to 1.2 hours for projecting video (in Eco Mode), and up to four hours as a speaker (it has built-in dual 3W JBL speakers). The auto keystone from XGIMI is one of the best ones I've experienced among all of the projectors I've tested, and it will adjust to practically any surface you cast it on, which can, with the 160° adjustable built-in stand, even be the ceiling. The current bundle brings an 80-inch screen included in the price.

In a recent development, if you have a bit more money to splurge, the MoGo 4 is the same concept as the Vibe One but takes its specs to the next level, and it's available starting at $359 (originally $499). It's still small and compact with 1080p resolution, but it nearly doubles the brightness, with 450 ISO lumens. The battery life more than doubles to two and a half hours in Eco Mode, while still keeping the projector under three pounds. It also has Google TV as its OS, but the projection is 360° with its adjustable built-in stand. You also have the option of getting the bundle with the PowerBase Stand, which extends the battery to five hours. Like the Vibe One, it has a built-in speaker, but this one uses dual 6W Harman Kardon speakers with Dolby Audio.The MoGo 4 Laser is a slightly upgraded version that uses triple laser technology for a better picture. It still supports 1080p resolution, but it's brighter with 550 ISO lumens and a 1000:1 contrast. The battery life, OS system, stand, speakers, and auto keystone technology are the same—but the bundles are different, so they're worth considering if they fit your needs.

Industry observers note that if you're looking for a premium portable projector, the Horizon 30 Pro is a great option that competes with the best options on the market. It supports 4K resolution, uses RGB triple laser brightness that reaches 4800 ISO lumens (bright enough to see during the day), has a 120Hz refresh rate and gaming features to make gaming smooth, displays an 8,000:1 native contrast to make colors and blacks pop, and supports IMAX Enhanced, Dolby Vision, and HDR10+. It has an adjustable stand like the other XGIMI projectors and its own dual 12W Harman Kardon speakers with DTS Virtual:X and DTS-HD. The auto keystone is just as powerful as the other options, but the lens adds an optical zoom and a Lens Memory feature, which lets you save up to six custom lens and image setups and recall them with a click. Right now, it's down to $1,899 (originally $2,499) after a 24% discount.

The Cutthroat Business of Shipwrecks

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jstor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in 1627, treasures started to wash up on the beaches of France: diamonds, ebony, precious porcelain, spices, ivory, ambergris, and bezoars.
  • In a recent development, the disaster swiftly threatened to become an international incident.
  • It has been revealed that it’s easy to understand why a beachcomber who found a diamond in the sand might want to hold onto it, but there was a legal basis for their claims.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in 1627, treasures started to wash up on the beaches of France: diamonds, ebony, precious porcelain, spices, ivory, ambergris, and bezoars. Two Portuguese ships, so huge they were referred to as “floating cities,” had shipwrecked off the coast of Bordeaux, spilling luxury goods into the waves.

In a recent development, the disaster swiftly threatened to become an international incident. The owners of the cargo (unsurprisingly) wanted their goods back—but the coast dwellers claimed that anything that washed up on shore was theirs by the ancient droit du naufrage, the “right of wreck.”.

It has been revealed that it’s easy to understand why a beachcomber who found a diamond in the sand might want to hold onto it, but there was a legal basis for their claims. The “right of wreck” was a long-lived and widespread custom, one that shaped the very architecture of seaside towns: in his travels through Norfolk, Daniel Defoe wrote that the “country people had scarce a barn, or a shed, or a stable…but what was built of old planks, beams, wales and timbers, &c. the wrecks of ships, and ruins of mariners and merchants’ fortunes.”.

That mentioned, in legal terms, the right of wreck was a little more complicated than “finders keepers.” In many places, it wasn’t actually the person who stumbled on the shipwrecked goods who held the right to them; rather, they became the property of the local lord. In the earliest iterations of this idea, poor shipwreck survivors could find themselves roughly stripped of all their goods—as King Richard I of England found when his fleet was unlucky enough to wash up off the coast of Cyprus, circa 1191. His fiancée and his sister were taken as captives by the emperor of the island, who also helped himself to all the treasure they’d been traveling with. (This didn’t end well for the emperor, who lost his throne in the ensuing war.).

Neither wealthy merchants nor traveling kings were particularly enthusiastic about the idea that an accident at sea could mean forfeiting all their cargo. On the other hand, powerful landowners were eager to preserve their right to the occasional random windfall. As international trade increased, the right of wreck was slowly reshaped by centuries of legal wrangling. Courts battling over who could keep what ended up creating, for instance, highly specific legal definitions for terms like “flotsam” (goods that just happened to float to the surface after a wreck) and “jetsam” (goods intentionally tossed from a ship to make it lighter).

It has been revealed that the resulting patchwork of rules meant that every shipwreck was a complex negotiation between competing interests. Usually, the owners of the shipwrecked goods were entitled to their property back, in exchange for some kind of fee. Whether that was a ransom or a fair reward for helping salvage the goods is a matter of perspective.

In a recent development, in 1236, King Henry III of England issued an edict stating that if “man, dog, or cat” escaped the shipwreck alive, finders were obligated to hold on to the wrecked goods for three months, allowing the survivors to claim them in that time. There is a bit of an issue with that rule: it’s easy to see how it could create an incentive for shore dwellers to do away with shipwreck survivors in order to claim their goods (whether those survivors be man, dog, or cat).

In a recent development, legends of these dark deeds swirled for centuries, but there’s little evidence they really happened. Still, people could be rough in their efforts to “salvage.” In Estonia, for instance, where the local lords were entitled to rewards if they helped to save ships in distress, people developed a habit of launching into enthusiastic “rescue” operations, whether or not there was any real danger.

Get your fix of JSTOR Daily’s best stories in your inbox each Thursday.

A particularly good wreck could spark a feeding frenzy. An account of the wreck of the Golden Grape in 1641 gives a sense of the chaos:.

In a recent development, the first arrivals on the beach contented themselves with staving in barrels and filling linen bags and pockets with raisins or, stripping off their waistcoats, used the sleeves as bags. But soon bands of men appeared from the various villages… Some gangs or men took away a score or two of barrels of raisins or the same number of jars of oil, but they were lucky if they did not have to share their booty with a stronger gang before they could gain a place of safety.

According to recent reports, not everything washes ashore, of course; many of the treasures lost in wrecks sank under the waves. There were fortunes to be made, but in a time before diving equipment, the trouble was how to reach it. In the early modern era, for the most part, even European sailors could hardly swim. But Africans living by the sea in Senegambia and the Gold Coast were highly skilled swimmers and divers—leading them to be targeted by enslavers, who knew their specialized skills could be turned to the recovery of underwater riches. As historian Kevin Dawson writes in “History Below the Waterline: Enslaved Salvage Divers Harvesting Seaports’ Hinter-Seas in the Early Modern Atlantic”:.

The African-honed expertise that enslaved underwater divers carried throughout the Atlantic world allowed them to rapidly recover several tons of gold, silver, and other items from shipwrecks, especially old Spanish treasure hulks. Possessing proficiencies held by few in the world, divers exchanged their unique ability to rapidly produce capital for semi-independent lives of privileged exploitation.

Recent findings suggest that their skills were so irreplaceable that they were able to negotiate for better treatment than most enslaved people, including a share of what they salvaged. Though, of course, a share isn’t much when you’re doing all the work.

#223149. Pimalaya goes stable: Himalaya v3 and the pimdir standard

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1920 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pimalaya ↗ Open Full Page

Pimalaya goes stable: Himalaya v3 and the pimdir standard

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1920 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pimalaya

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It took months, but here we are: the whole Pimalaya CLI family is released at once, at the top of the first stable version of the pimdir standard.
  • According to recent reports, most of them are majors, and they all break something for somebody.
  • Sources indicate that in Another year with NLnet I said this year was about consolidation and about a standard for PIM on disk.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took months, but here we are: the whole Pimalaya CLI family is released at once, at the top of the first stable version of the pimdir standard. Here the list:.

According to recent reports, most of them are majors, and they all break something for somebody. This post explains why, how, and where it goes from here. It is long, feel free to jump to the tool you care about.

Sources indicate that in Another year with NLnet I said this year was about consolidation and about a standard for PIM on disk. This release is the result of both.

The thing is, every piece is now connected:.

It has been revealed that releasing them one by one meant releasing tools that disagree with each other: one version of the store here, another version of the output there. So I decided to bring every tool to release level first, then to release them all together. It took way longer than I wanted, but this way what you install today is one coherent family.

The other reason is the contract. The CLIs are not only used by humans anymore: they are used by scripts, by frontends (the Vim plugin, the TUI, the Android app), and by AI agents through MCP. All of them need a stable, versioned contract: the same JSON shapes, the same error codes, the same exit codes. Majors are the right moment to fix it, and from now on it should not move anymore without a new major.

Few things made this release possible.

Specs before code. Every repository has a cairn/ folder holding its living spec, its change proposals and a dated log. Every behaviour change goes through a proposal, then gets folded into the spec. This way the truth is written somewhere, and not only in my head.

According to recent reports, one shared kit. The pimalaya-cli and pimalaya-config libs hold everything the CLIs have in common: the output contract, the error codes, the REPL, the MCP server, the configuration loading. In fact most of the work of this release was moving code from the CLIs into this kit, and deleting the copies.

One unified API, as a union. Before, the commands shared by every backend were the intersection of what the backends could do: if one backend could not do it, nobody could. Now it is the union: each backend registers the capabilities it really serves, with the same observable result as the others, and a command an account cannot serve fails before even connecting, with a clear capability-missing code.

Sources indicate that measured gates for pimdir. Audits always find something, so "no new finding" never ends. Instead, I built a test generator that produces stores, remote states and an oracle from a seed, and ran campaigns of 4,180 jobs against io-pimdir: crashes injected at every step, the search index checked against a full rebuild after each event, the sync engine replayed against scripted servers. The rule was simple: 2 campaigns in a row without any spec break, then freeze. Campaign 1 found one, campaigns 2 and 3 were clean, a late fix restarted the count, then campaigns 4 and 5 were clean. Freeze.

It has been revealed that live tests on real providers. Every CLI was tested against real accounts: Google, Microsoft, Fastmail and iCloud, plus few Chinese providers for Himalaya (QQ, 163, 139). A last "live night" just before the release found few bugs that went straight into the libs.

According to recent reports, libs first, apps after. The libs were released between the 13th and the 25th of November, the apps then moved to them without any patch or git pin. Everything you install comes from crates.io.

pimdir is a local-first standard for personal information: mails, contacts, calendars, tasks and files in one portable store, kept as a replica of every source, and searchable with one query language. A store is one SQLite file plus a content-addressed blob directory, the same on every OS and architecture. I already explained why such a standard is needed in Another year with NLnet, and how the Android app became its first full implementation in Pimalaya for Android enters closed alpha.

It comes in 3 parts, versioned separately:.

They are released together because a store holds sync state that follows the sync part, and the query language binds every program that offers search.

According to recent reports, what v1 means: schema version 1 never changes, every schema change is a migration, and a minor version only adds test cases. You can implement it in any language that speaks SQLite, use the I/O-free core of io-pimdir (like the Android app does, on the platform SQLite), or use its std client.

According to recent reports, few days before the freeze, I compared it with notmuch, which is the reference in this area. They do not do the same job (notmuch indexes mail files it does not own, pimdir owns the bodies, syncs them and holds other domains), but the search can be compared. On a store of 1 million messages from the Enron corpus, pimdir was ahead of notmuch on 50 of the 51 query measures and tied the last one, imported the million faster, and used a third of the memory. Stemming, regex and per-thread queries are still missing, they are on the list.

Industry observers note that one warning for the early adopters: a store written by a draft version is refused, never migrated. Sync it till nothing is pending with the last draft binary, move its directory aside, then let a release create and sync a newly introduced one.

This is the change many of you will not like, so let me explain it properly.

Every CLI had a configuration wizard: you typed your email address, it discovered the servers, asked for the password, stored it in your keyring, and wrote the TOML for you. It is gone, from every CLI.

It has been revealed that the direction. The CLIs are now low-level tools: plain text to glance at, JSON for scripts, frontends and agents. Comfort (tables, colours, relative dates, guided setups, rich composition) belongs to frontends. In fact this is not newly introduced: it is the same split that started the whole project, back when the logic left the Vim plugin. The CLI was always supposed to be the backend a frontend needs. This release just goes all the way.

I know some of you used the wizard to get started, and that copying a sample feels like a step back. If the welcome or the samples are not clear enough, it is a bug: please open an issue, I would rather fix the docs than bring back a second setup system per CLI.

Himalaya is now a low-level CLI over a unified mail API: the same commands on every backend, the protocol-specific ones next to them, plain text for a glance and --json for the rest.

Backends: IMAP, SMTP, ManageSieve, JMAP, the Gmail API, Microsoft Graph, Maildir (with a latest maildir++ layout for Dovecot and Courier stores), mbox, and pimdir. The README has recipes for Proton Mail (through Bridge), Fastmail, Gmail, Outlook, Posteo and iCloud.

Sources indicate that what is gone: the wizard, the m2dir backend (superseded by pimdir), the table and colour options, HIMALAYA_CONFIG. Unknown configuration keys are now refused, JSON keys are camelCase, and the v2 search syntax needs to be rewritten. The migration guide lists everything, with a full table for the queries.

Sources indicate that neverest is rebuilt around the pimdir store: every account syncs into one shared store, which the other CLIs read, search and queue their writes into. It syncs mails, contacts and calendars over IMAP, Gmail, Microsoft Graph, Google Calendar, Google People, CalDAV and CardDAV.

According to recent reports, JMAP sources are not supported yet (it is a draft), so Fastmail syncs over IMAP, CardDAV and CalDAV for now. Coming from v0.x? Your configuration and state are not carried over: start from the config.sample.toml, then run neverest sync --init.

The first stable release of Cardamum: a low-level CLI over a unified contacts API, with the same commands on CardDAV, JMAP, Microsoft Graph, Google People, vdir and pimdir.

card search speaks the pimdir query language on every backend, account capability demonstrates what an account serves without connecting, and you get the REPL and the MCP server like the others. Editing a card is left to a composer such as tcard. The wizard and the discover route are gone.

Same story for calendars: the same commands on CalDAV, JMAP (newly introduced), Google Calendar, Microsoft Graph, vdir and pimdir.

Industry observers note that fresh: event search, recurrence expansion, attendees and alarms, online meetings (--online-meeting), invitation replies through pimdir, and an agenda that draws a month or a year like cal(1) does. Editing an event is left to a composer such as tcal. The wizard, the tables and colours, and the todo and journal commands are gone: tasks and journals will move to dedicated tools (Unfog and Journal), not released yet.

In a recent development, carillon is a local watcher that fires hooks on what changes in your mailboxes, address books and calendars, over IMAP, JMAP, Maildir, CalDAV, CardDAV, Microsoft Graph, the Google APIs and the pimdir store. It uses push where the server offers it (IMAP IDLE, the JMAP event stream) and polls elsewhere. A hook runs a command, shows a desktop notification, or both.

New in v1: a pimdir backend, on-alarm-trigger for the alarms of events and tasks, on-birthday-trigger for birthdays and anniversaries, a per-hook timeout, and a report of what moved while an IMAP or Gmail session was lost. Hooks now take the same shape as Comodoro's.

Ortie manages OAuth tokens for the other tools. v3 aligns it on the rest of the family: ready-made Google, Microsoft and Fastmail accounts to paste, token revocation, an auth listen to catch a redirection handed off from another machine, account checks, a REPL, and an MCP server that never hands the token to the agent. The wizard and the hooks are gone (the storage write command does what a hook did).

Comodoro manages timers: one server owns a timer, any number of clients drive it, over a local socket or TCP. v3 joins the same standard: comodoro watch feeds a status bar without polling, hooks get the cycle name and duration, plus the welcome, account checks, a REPL and an MCP server. Comodoro is now a binary only: the library is gone, and the open JSON-RPC protocol is the contract for third parties.

None of the above would exist without the libs below, all released in November on crates.io:.

They are all I/O-free, as usual: feel free to build your own tools at the top of them.

Each README lists the ways to install: prebuilt binaries from the GitHub releases (or the install.sh script), cargo install --locked, Nix, and the APT, DNF and Homebrew repositories at pkg.pimalaya.org. The packages are landing there over the coming days, and the nixpkgs and home-manager updates are on their way.

Industry observers note that special thanks to the NLnet foundation and the European Commission's NGI initiative, for the financial support through NGI Zero Core and now the NGI Zero Commons Fund. This kind of slow, deep work is only possible thanks to them.

And thank you to everyone who reported bugs, tested betas, or simply waited patiently while everything was being rebuilt. Any feedback is welcomed, on GitHub, on Matrix or on Mastodon. Let me know how it goes!

Sources indicate that shark and Dyson are two of the biggest names in vacuums — but which one is better? Which one makes the best vacuum? I've tested Dysons, Samsungs, Ultenics, and I've previously owned Sharks. So let's get to the bottom of the best-value vacuum cleaner, especially considering it's Black Friday — A.K.A. the best time to buy upcoming tech.

Today, I'm going to help you decide between six of the most popular Shark and Dyson vacuums, starting from just $189. What's a HEPA filter? Do you need a laser eye? What about suction power? What does RPM actually mean?

I'll help you get to the bottom of it all — and hopefully you'll leave knowing precisely which vacuum cleaner to invest in this Black Friday. So long, dusty carpets and crumbly floors!

Unfortunately, Shark doesn't list its suction power, but all of these models automatically monitor floor type and adjust power for hardwood and carpeted surfaces.

The Shark Power Pro Reveal Plus is the cheapest option on this list; it automatically adjusts suction power for hardwood and carpet, has an LED headlight to illuminate every speck of dust, and lasts for up to 40 minutes.

The Shark Power Detect Pet Plus Clean & Empty lasts for a huge 70 minutes on one charge, adjusts suction power for hardwood and carpeted floors, and even automatically empties itself with the emptying station.

The Shark Power Detect Speed Plus Clean & Empty is only discounted in oatmeal (pictured), lasts for 60 minutes on a single charge, and, like the Power Detect Pet Plus Clean & Empty, automatically empties and charges itself with the included station.

Dyson's vacuums tend to be pricier than Shark's, but Dyson publishes each model's RPM and air wattage so you know exactly how powerful the vacuums are before you buy.

With 40 mins of battery life, 100 air watts of suction, and a 120,000 RPM motor, the Dyson V9 is a powerful and lightweight vacuum for everyday cleaning.

It has been revealed that A level up from the V9, the V10 offers 60 minutes of battery life, 150 air watts of suction, and even has a 125,000 RPM motor. The Konical Variant is also $329 and has a green laser to illuminate dust.

The most expensive model on this list, the Dyson V15 Detect boasts 60 minutes of runtime, a green laser to illuminate dust, 240 air watts of suction power, and a 125,000-RPM motor.

Shark Power Detect Pet Plus Clean & Empty.

Shark Power Detect Speed Plus Clean & Empty.

Sources indicate that the best-value model on this list is far and away the Shark Power Pro Reveal Plus. Right now, this stick vacuum is just $179, which is $90 cheaper than Dyson's cheapest, the V9 Motobar.

Although Shark doesn't publish its air wattage, it would be a fine vacuum for everyday cleaning. The battery lasts for 40 minutes on eco mode; usually, stick vacuums go for around ten minutes on full power. This Shark model also has an LED light, which is a feature I look for on every vacuum. Now that I've used a vacuum with an LED light, I can't ever go back — it's so much easier to spot pesky dirty patches with a light.

According to recent reports, neither of the other Shark models offer an LED light, which is disappointing to see — but they do both have automatic bin emptying and charging. If you often forget to empty or charge your stick vacuum, you might want to check out these two models (Power Detect Pet and Power Detect Speed).

If you can afford it, I'd also recommend the Dyson V10 Cyclone. If you get the Konical Variant, which is $329, it has a green laser light to illuminate all patches of dirt.

The priciest option on this list is the Dyson V15 Detect, $598, but has the highest-rated air wattage for the most powerful suction.

Personally, I would buy the Dyson V10 Konical variant as I can't live without the green laser. At $329, 150 air watts of suction and 125,000RPM motor power is a sweet deal.

These are the best over-ear headphones I tested in 2025 (or ever, really). Right now, you can get the WH-1000XM6 headphones for $348 (originally $459.99), their lowest price ever during the early Black Friday sale from Amazon.

Recent findings suggest that the XM6 headphones improve on what were already excellent headphones. Sony upped the count of microphones from eight to 12 when compared to the XM5, which improves more than just how well you sound to someone on a phone call. The microphones are used in almost all of its features, like ANC, Adaptive Sound Control, and the headphones' Ambient Sound mode. They hear your surroundings to adapt their features accordingly. If you switch from a noisy room to a quiet one, the XM6 can switch from ANC to "aware mode" (if you have Adaptive Sound Control on).

Mike Leigh has a few regrets, but declining to work with Hollywood actors isn’t one of them.

In an interview with The Guardian, the decorated British director reminded the world why his unusual methods mean he’s happy sticking with British character actors. He “snorted” at the idea of casting big Hollywood movie stars.

Recent findings suggest that “Well, first of all let’s clear up what’s involved in doing that,” he mentioned. “You – the name actor – would have to commit yourself to the project for months on end. You may have to get out in the real world and do some research. You may not be playing a character that squares with your idea of how you want to be seen; the idealised version of your own personality.” Related Stories Trailers 'Tender Loving Care' Upcoming Trailer: Mike Leigh's Latest Is A Meditation On Love & Growing Old News Gotham Awards Film Nominations Led By 'The Invite', 'Tender Loving Care', 'All Of A Sudden' & More.

Leigh added: “If someone were to say, ‘The reason you fucked up and failed is because you didn’t get star names’, then in all humility I’d accept it. But that simply isn’t the case.” Watch on Deadline.

Leigh’s methods are collaborative and involve developing scripts with actors as filming progresses. His new movie, Tender Loving Care, features his long-time partner Marion Bailey and Widow’s Bay star Kate O’Flynn. The film follows Amy (O’Flynn), who, after a bitter breakup, moves in with her best friend, Rosie (Alice Bailey Johnson). Both work as social workers in London, at opposite ends of the age spectrum. Rosie becomes like a second daughter to Amy’s parents, notably her elderly father, who is starting to show his age.

Having made bigger period films like Peterloo and Mr. Turner in recent years, the 83-year-old Palme d’Or winner did say he regrets never making a big budget modern-day film with a “broad canvas and a contemporary subject.”.

He was promoting Tender Loving Care, which he has frequently mentioned will be his last directing gig. This is because he has a debilitating condition, myositis, which has made the physical demands of directing difficult as it has weakened his muscles and restricted his movement.

“I’m now very seasoned in listening to everybody in the world telling me why and how I can keep working. And my answer to that begins with an ‘F’ and ends with an ‘off’,” joked Leigh.

He insisted he isn’t retiring and instead will “sit down and write something.”.

From WhatsApp’s blog post announcing support for scheduled messages:.

You can write a message when you think of it and send it anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both your 1:1 and group chats.

To schedule a message, press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. It will look like any other message to the person receiving it. You can see all future messages you have lined up, and delete them beforehand if you change your mind.

Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us.

WhatsApp notes this feature is “rolling out globally over the coming weeks.” So you might not see it right away, but even if you don’t, it should show up on your account soon.

Scheduled messages work not only for text, but also when sending media like photos and videos.

To get access to scheduled messages, make sure you’ve updated to the latest WhatsApp app enhancement, which was just released today.

In a recent development, northern Ireland Screen has appointed its newly introduced Chief Executive. Laura Livingstone will take on the role in January.

Livingstone will take over from current CEO Richard Williams, who revealed in June that he would step down from the role in December after over 23 years in the position.

The exec has two decades of experience across film, TV, VFX and creative technology. Formerly a Netflix VFX executive, she is currently a VFX producer on an Amazon MGM Studios series. Sources indicate that speaking about her new role at Northern Ireland’s lead screen agency, Livingstone said: “I am delighted and honoured to have been appointed CEO of Northern Ireland Screen. Northern Ireland has an extraordinary wealth of creative talent and has established an international reputation for excellence across the screen industries. That success is a testament to the work of Richard Williams, the Northern Ireland Screen team and the wider industry.

She continued: “Having worked internationally for many years, I am incredibly excited to bring that experience home. I look forward to working with the team and our partners to build on these strong foundations, champion our homegrown talent, embrace latest opportunities and ensure Northern Ireland continues to thrive as a place where great stories are created and told.”.

Sir David Sterling, Chair of Northern Ireland Screen, added: “On behalf of Northern Ireland Screen, I warmly welcome Laura as our new Chief Executive. Laura brings with her a wealth of experience in the screen industry and her expertise will guide Northern Ireland Screen into its next chapter. I would also like to express our sincere gratitude to our outgoing CEO, Richard Williams, for his exceptional leadership of Northern Ireland Screen and more than 23 years of dedicated service to the organisation.”.

I was excited for Garmin Fenix 8 Pro deals this Black Friday, and knew the Fenix 8 would also be on sale, but I did not expect Garmin to cut the price of the Fenix 9 Pro too, because it only came out a couple of months ago.

I’ve tested all three watches extensively, running marathons with the Fenix 8 and Fenix 8 Pro and using the Fenix 9 Pro for the past couple of months after its launch, and all three have their merits in the sales.

Which you go for depends on a few key factors, relating to the design options and some select features that are only on the newer models.

Below I’ve highlighted what I think the key differences are between the watches, to hopefully help you make a call on which to buy.

The main reason to get the oldest Fenix of the trio is value, because it comes in $100 cheaper than the Fenix 8 Pro on sale, even when opting for a sapphire titanium model.

However, it’s not the only reason, because the orange Garmin Fenix 8 on sale is actually one of the best-looking Garmins ever made, in my opinion, and also a little bit thinner than the newer Fenix models.

The Fenix 8 offers the best value of the three latest Fenixes on sale, and only misses out on a few key features compared to the newer watches. You don't get LTE and satellite connectivity or quite as bright an AMOLED display, but it still nails the essentials of sports tracking and navigation, and does so for $100 less than the Fenix 8 Pro.

As you’d expect, you miss out on some features by getting the Fenix 8, most notably the LTE and satellite connectivity available on the newer Pro models.

It also has a slightly less bright AMOLED display, which I can’t say I’ve noticed too much in my testing, and lacks the green flashlight setting and faster maps on the Fenix 9 Pro.

Garmin is actually rolling back most of the software features that arrived on the Fenix 9 Pro to the Fenix 8, though, and in general it matches the upcoming watches well for key sports tracking, training analysis, battery life, and navigation features.

I really don’t think you lose out on too much by getting the Fenix 8 myself, and there are three size options to pick between, along with the choice of an AMOLED or MIP display.

The main reason I’d choose the Garmin Fenix 8 Pro over the Fenix 8 is its connectivity features, which can be a lifesaver if you regularly venture off the grid or like to leave your phone behind during activities.

Getting those features while saving $150 compared with the Fenix 9 Pro makes the Fenix 8 Pro a tempting option for adventurers.

Aside from the more attractive, all-titanium design, green flashlight, and faster maps on the Fenix 9 Pro, the Fenix 8 Pro really does match up well with the newer watch on features, and you can get it for $150 less in the sales.

However, the Fenix 8 Pro only comes in AMOLED (or MicroLED, but that’s still wildly expensive) and 47mm and 51mm sizes, so those looking for a 43mm or MIP watch will have to opt for the Fenix 8 or Fenix 9 instead.

If you have to have the latest and greatest smartwatch on your wrist, it’s the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro, and the fact that it’s reduced at all is a pleasant surprise this Black Friday.

The main upgrade on the Fenix 8 Pro is the all-titanium design of the Fenix 9 Pro, which I have to say is incredibly attractive and a bigger enhancement than I expected.

In a recent development, all models of the Garmin Fenix 9 are reduced by at least $100 for Black Friday, including the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro with InReach, which is the watch I'm using as my main tracker right now. If you want the latest and greatest Garmin watch, this is the time to buy it, because it's the first time it's been discounted anywhere.

You also get a green flashlight mode, which I do now use more often than the white mode as it doesn’t ruin your night vision, and faster panning and zooming with maps.

As it’s the newest watch, the Fenix 9 Pro will also be getting software updates further into the future than the Fenix 8 and Fenix 8 Pro, though Garmin has shown more willingness to roll back upgrades to older models recently.

You can save $100 on any model of the Fenix 9 Pro, which has MIP and AMOLED options in its lineup, plus three sizes, and there’s actually one Fenix 9 model that’s reduced even further, which is the 43mm Fenix 9.

In a recent development, this sneaky little deal on one color of the 43mm Garmin Fenix 9 makes it the cheapest model of the latest watch available by $50. It misses out on some upgrades you do get on the Fenix 9 Pro, but given that the Fenix 8 Pro only comes in 47mm and 51mm sizes, this is the best 43mm Fenix you can get for $849.

The standard Fenix 9 doesn’t have the all-titanium build or extra connectivity of the Pro models (or the green flashlight mode), so I think the Fenix 8 Pro is better value at the same price, but this is the cheapest you’ll find Garmin’s latest flagship anywhere.

#223136. Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email
