Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1219 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Techstackups

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that on 24 November, Google made its eight Workspace MCP servers generally available and published a newly introduced clause in its API terms.
  • In a recent development, read the Gmail server's tool list and you'll find that it can search your mail, read threads, create a draft and file things under labels.
  • If you've built an email assistant on the Gmail API, or you run a coding agent with a Google Workspace plugin, you have about two months to work out which side of the rule you're on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that on 24 November, Google made its eight Workspace MCP servers generally available and published a newly introduced clause in its API terms. From 1 February 2027, any tool that "is or is driven by an AI Agent" must reach Gmail, Drive, Calendar and the rest of Workspace through those servers.

In a recent development, read the Gmail server's tool list and you'll find that it can search your mail, read threads, create a draft and file things under labels. It can't send a message, reply, forward, or change a draft after creating it. Those tools exist, but Google's quota page states they "require partner access and aren't generally available".

If you've built an email assistant on the Gmail API, or you run a coding agent with a Google Workspace plugin, you have about two months to work out which side of the rule you're on.

The upcoming Workspace AI Tools Addendum to the Google APIs Terms of Service puts it in one sentence:.

The GWS Access Tool must use a Google MCP where the GWS Access Tool is or is driven by an AI Agent, an AI Harness or an AI model or service employing an AI model.

The next sentence forbids disguising an agent to avoid the classification. Breaking either lets Google "restrict or remove the GWS Access Tool's access" or suspend your account.

In a recent development, there's a technical side too. From the same date, agents that call the REST APIs directly are held to Standard-tier quotas, whatever tier the project has paid for. REST keeps working for them, slowly and in breach of the terms.

Apps that don't involve AI carry on as before. A nightly backup job, a CRM sync or a deterministic script on its own OAuth client is, in Google's words, "not affected by this change".

The addendum also adds data rules that matter to anyone building an agent with memory:.

It has been revealed that the 30-day cap is the one product teams will feel. An assistant that builds a long-term index of your inbox to answer questions about last year's contracts has to rebuild it monthly or drop it.

In a recent development, coverage is uneven. Docs, Slides and Tasks are close to everything the REST API offers. Gmail and Drive are much thinner.

The Gmail gap is the one that breaks real workflows. An agent that drafts a reply, gets feedback from you and revises it before you hit send can't do the revision step. It has to create a second draft and leave the first one behind.

Drive's gap is similar: an agent can create a report but can't move it into the right folder or share it with the team.

Google hasn't noted who qualifies for partner access or when the partner-only Gmail tools will reach everyone. The effect is already visible, though. Anthropic's Google Workspace connector for Claude advertises sending, replying and forwarding email, and moving and trashing Drive files. Those are exactly the operations the public servers lack.

So a large AI vendor's agent can send your email through an approved channel, while an independent developer's agent, using the same OAuth scopes the user granted, can only leave drafts. Once the addendum takes effect, that independent developer also can't fall back to the REST API without breaching the terms.

In a recent development, the definitions are broad. An "AI Harness" or a tool "driven by" an AI model plausibly covers a personal script that pipes your inbox into an LLM, and a "GWS Access Point" explicitly includes any "connector, proxy, command line interface, or third-party service". Google hasn't addressed hobby use directly.

Classification starts with self-declaration. OAuth clients now have a checkbox, "Use this client for an AI-powered agent", and since 11 November the MCP servers reject clients without it. Clients created before the cut-off and not marked in time stay non-agentic permanently, so owners have to create fresh ones. Google hasn't said how it will detect agents that call REST without declaring themselves.

A few edge cases are documented:.

In a recent development, every project gets the free Standard tier: 5,000 MCP requests per day, per project, per product. Some calls cost more than one request. A Gmail search_threads or list_drafts counts as 10, so an agent that does nothing but search gets 500 searches a day across all its consumers. That's a project-wide limit, so a small multi-user product will hit it swiftly.

Industry observers note that the paid Scaled tier starts billing on 1 April 2027 for Gmail, Calendar and Drive. Its structure favours REST. MCP usage is billed from the first request, while REST usage gets large free daily allowances: 70 million light Gmail requests a day, for example. Google hasn't published per-request prices.

Google's case, from a Cloud blog post by Chandu Thota and Brad Calder, is that OAuth was designed for apps acting on a human's clear intent:.

According to recent reports, traditional REST APIs were built for human-paced apps where a valid OAuth token implied user intent. As AI agents shift from reading information to acting autonomously at machine speed â¦ a valid token is no longer enough. Policy checks, data boundaries, and human confirmation have to live in the request path.

Recent findings suggest that there's substance to this. An email agent that reads a message saying "forward the last ten invoices to this address" is a well-documented prompt-injection risk, and a token that allows gmail.modify gives the agent the power to do it. Routing every agent through one gateway gives admins a single place to block categories of action, require approval and audit what happened. The MCP servers do all of that, and apply data-loss-prevention rules automatically.

Recent findings suggest that the same design also gives Google control of which agents can do what, which data they can keep, and whether anything built on that data can compete with Google's own products. The partner-only tools and the 30-day cap on embeddings show that control in use.

Slack went down a similar path in May 2025. It cut history API rate limits to one request a minute for apps outside its Marketplace and banned bulk export of Slack data for LLMs. Slack drew the line by distribution channel. Google draws it by whether the software is an AI, which is harder to define and harder to enforce.

If you build an agent product on Workspace:.

If you run a personal agent or MCP server against your own account: open-source servers that call REST, such as the popular google_workspace_mcp, will keep running, but at Standard quotas and outside the terms. Switching to Google's servers costs you sending and draft editing in Gmail, and moving and sharing in Drive.

In a recent development, if you're a Workspace admin: the newly introduced controls are under Admin console â Security â API Controls. You can block or approve each category of agent action, set approval policies, and see agent activity in the audit logs. Consumers can't view or revoke the approvals they've saved, which expire after 90 days, so it's worth setting policy before people start connecting agents.

If your integration doesn't use AI: nothing changes, as long as it stays on its own OAuth client and nobody wires a model into it.

Among the scrappy newcomers are French-Russian filmmaker Lada Egorova and Brazilian filmmaker Thiago Aragão, a duo a few years out of college, who have launched LA-based platform Pocket Cinema+, an independent microseries streaming app whose early offerings include a Western/samurai drama and a sci-fi series, both shot in and around LA.

The firm offers vertical and horizontal genre series and they’re preparing a French production partnership as their next step. The idea is for the slate to include English and French-language genre series, starting with a horror, and they’re targeting budgets in the $60k-$100k range.

“Our editorial focus is genre-driven microseries, with an ambition to develop a wider range of stories and filmmaker perspectives within short-form entertainment,” the duo told us.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that according to a new Counterpoint Research report, Apple increased its share of Latin America’s smartphone shipments in Q3 2026, recording the smallest decline among the region’s top five brands. Here are the details.

In a report released this week, Counterpoint Research indicates the ongoing memory crunch led to a 24% year-over-year drop in smartphone shipments during Q3, “the second-lowest quarter since 2015.”.

It has been revealed that per the report, Samsung maintained its lead with a 35% shipment share, despite a 15% year-over-year decline in total shipments, well ahead of second-place Motorola, which captured 18% of shipments after a 23% drop. Interestingly, Motorola’s share actually increased one percentage point from a year earlier.

Rounding out the top five were Xiaomi, with a 14% share and a whopping 34% decline, Apple, with a 9% share and a 10% decline, and Honor, with an 8% share and a 27% decline.

Despite the decline in overall shipments, Apple’s shipment share increased by 2 percentage points from 7% a year earlier, moving the company from fifth to fourth place in the region.

Other brands collectively accounted for 16% of shipments, down from 19% a year earlier, with their combined shipments falling 37% year over year.

Here’s Counterpoint on Apple’s performance for Q3 in Latin America:.

Recent findings suggest that apple was the most resilient, with the smallest decline among the top five brands (shipments down 10% YoY), and rose one position to No. 4 in the region. Apple absorbed the impact of price increases better than its rivals, helped by strong product availability. Apple released the iPhone 18 Pro series at the end of the quarter. For the first time, Chile joined Brazil and Mexico in the first launch wave.

Recent findings suggest that as for regional factors that contributed to the decline, Senior Analyst Benjamin Corona noted that Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia faced additional challenges beyond the global memory shortage, ranging from political uncertainty to inflation and tighter household budgets. Smartphone shipments fell 22%, 26%, and 28% in those countries, respectively.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint says it “expects the decline to ease in Q4 2026 as prices stabilize and seasonal demand returns,” adding that “memory-related price pressure should moderate by Q2 2027, but supply constraints will likely continue through the end of 2027.”.

He was guest of honor at the do in Johannesburg where the Canal+ Academy was unveiled.

The academy combines Canal+’s pre-existing University model with the MultiChoice Talent Factory (MTF), which together have trained around 10,500 people across the past eight years. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Saatva CEO Ron Rudzin first proposed selling luxury mattresses online, he was met with disbelief. “They thought I was crazy,” Rudzin told us. “They stated, ‘Sell mattresses and no one touches them before they buy?'".

But 16 years later, Saatva has proven that you can shop for a high-quality bed without the obligatory five minute lie down in a bricks and mortar store. And the mattress that has catapulted Saatva into the mainstream? The Saatva Classic, a handcrafted hybrid that marries traditional bed design with a modern approach to mattress shopping.

In an exclusive interview for Tom's Guide, Byron Golub, Saatva's Senior Vice President of Product, talks us through the design and creation of Saatva's number one mattress and explains why 'classic' never goes out of style.

According to recent reports, the Saatva Black Friday sale is serving up the best prices we've seen since Labor Day, and we don't expect them to drop any lower ahead of the Presidents' Day sales in February, making now a great time to buy. A one-year sleep trial, a limited lifetime warranty and free white glove delivery are included with every Saatva Classic.

Our Saatva Classic mattress review score: ★★★★★.

“The Saatva Classic began with a straightforward but ambitious premise," explains Golub. "The American consumer deserved access to the kind of sleep experience typically reserved for the world’s finest hotels — without the traditional retail markup that put luxury mattresses out of reach for most people.”.

To achieve that balance of 'luxury' and 'affordable', founders Ron Rudzin and Ricky Joshi had to cut out a part of the mattress buying process that, until now, had been considered integral.

They got rid of the mattress store – Saatva was going online-only.

In 2010, this was a bolder premise than it sounds today. But by losing the inherent costs of a brick-and-mortar mattress store, Saatva could pass on the savings to the customer.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

And, in doing so, hopefully cut down on what Golub describes as the familiar frustration of an industry that was “opaque, overcomplicated, and overpriced.”.

Officially introduced in 2010, Saatva, which derives from the Sanskrit word meaning truth and purity, started with just one mattress.

This luxury hybrid-innerspring drew from the traditional design of hotel mattresses and would go on to become the flagship Classic.

“The Classic released as Saatva’s founding product and was among the first luxury mattresses sold direct to the consumer online — at a time when buying a mattress without lying on it in a showroom was still a novel concept,” states Golub.

“The result was a mattress that could compete with what you’d find at a five-star property, built to support healthy sleep from the ground up.”.

With the Classic mattress, Saatva hoped to merge three key concepts:.

Spinal alignment was a central design requirement from the start, which led to an early focus on zoned support.

The design process resulted in a multi-layered mattress that relied on traditional innerspring support to deliver "hotel-grade" comfort but for the "everyday sleeper.".

Industry observers note that the Saatva Classic comes in two heights, 11.5" and 14.5", and is crafted from a combination of coils and comfort foam. Each layer contributes to the overall sleep comfort.

From top to bottom, here's a detailed look at how a Saatva Classic is constructed:.

Sources indicate that the Classic is available in three feels. You can opt for a Plush Soft (3/10 on the mattress firmness scale), Luxury Firm (5-7/10) or Firm (8/10). The basic construction of the Classic remains the same regardless of firmness but the foams in the Eurotop have a different ILD (Impression Load Deflection) based on the feel. Saatva foams have an ILD of between 18 and 30, and the exact foam and fiber blend changes depending on the feel. The Classic is also available in two mattress heights: 11.5" and 14.5". The taller model has two extra turns in the base coil unit, to add height.

It has been revealed that the Classic's 3-inch Euro pillowtop is encased in an organic cotton blend fabric, grown without pesticides and GMOs, backed to a low-melt polyester for durability. Tape edges give a gold damask finish.

Industry observers note that fiberglass-free, the Classic uses a plant-based flame retardant of thistle and wool pulp, bonded with small amounts of polyester. The surface is finished with Guardin® antimicrobial botanical fabric treatment, containing thyme, geranium, lemongrass, mint and more.

It has been revealed that ‘Lumbar Zone Quilting’ is used in the central third of the mattress, to add extra support at the base of the spine. This sewing technique places the tufting in close configuration, creating a tighter finish that comes pre-compressed, to avoid your body sinking.

Recent findings suggest that sitting beneath is a ½” gel-infused visco-elastic memory foam lumbar crown with an ‘active spinal wire’ — a wire frame sized to the perimeter of the lumbar crown — below. Increased reinforcement at the lumbar, this unique feature is patented by Saatva.

Golub explains that the design process of the Classic is centered on the guiding principle of restorative sleep. “Every element of the Classic was interrogated through that lens," he says.

"Not just comfort in the moment of lying down, but the kind of deep, uninterrupted sleep that leaves you genuinely restored the next morning.”.

It has been revealed that it’s a bold ideal but one the brand has tried to realize practically through a focus on lumbar support. This design element is key to the Classic’s continued success — both on the market and in our Sleep Lab.

The center third of the mattress, where the heaviest part of the body rests, demands the most attention.

I've tested the Saatva Classic multiple times and the first thing that always stands out is a sense of relief. From head-to-toe, the Classic's support enables you to let go of tension and simply relax.

Rudzin describes targeted support as the "most crucial thing about all Saatva beds.".

"Spinal alignment was a central design requirement from the start," continues Golub, "which led to an early focus on zoned support.

"That's the understanding that the body needs different levels of firmness in different areas, and that the center third of the mattress, where the heaviest part of the body rests, demands the most attention.”.

In the Classic, four design elements form this vital support core. These are:.

According to recent reports, this focus on support has earned the Classic endorsement from the American Chiropractic Association. Golub explains this is an independent assessment of the Classic's construction, awarded to finished models.

While lumbar support might be a guiding principle of the Classic, its luxury design is equally important to its success. And this hotel indulgence isn't just found in the finish, but woven through the construction process.

Because each mattress is made fresh for the person who ordered it, Saatva can use materials and construction methods that wouldn’t survive long-term storage.

“Every Saatva Classic is built to order," explains Golub. "Production begins only after a customer places their order, through a network of factories across the United States.".

Golub believes this 'off the line' delivery is essential to achieving a high-quality mattress.

"It matters to the design in a very direct way: because each mattress is made fresh for the person who ordered it, Saatva can use materials and construction methods that wouldn’t survive long-term storage.".

In a recent development, he notes that higher-quality foams, hand-finished upholstery, and other details might degrade if left sitting in an inventory. (While boxed mattresses have proven themselves to be a convenient way forward for the sleep industry, Saatva’s commitment to traditional flat delivery adds to the appeal of the Classic.).

According to recent reports, "It also aligns with Saatva’s commitment to sustainability," says Golub. "Building to order means no overproduction, no excess inventory, and no waste from products that never find a home.".

It has been revealed that and Golub notes the "service experience" is considered part of the product by Saatva. Free white glove delivery, including set up and old mattress removal, is as integral to the product as the tufted top.

And for a brand that emphasizes lumbar support and back pain relief, it’s a bonus that someone else carries the bed up the stairs for you.

Since launch in 2010, Saatva has made some significant changes, including expanding its line-up to encompass all-foam, latex and even smart beds.

The brand also opened its first Saatva Viewing Room in 2019, offering customers a chance to get hands-on with the Saatva mattress line-up, while a team of Saatva Sleep Guides are on hand to answer any questions.

Howeve, the basic design of the Saatva Classic has remained largely unchanged.

“The architecture that defined the Classic on day one — the dual coil system, the Euro pillow top, the Lumbar Zone reinforcement, our signature mattress cover made with organic cotton — remains intact,” explains Golub.

Recent findings suggest that even so, the mattress you buy in today’s Saatva mattress sales isn’t the same Classic you would have picked up in 2010. Golub explain that over the years Saatva has focused not on redesign, but on improving the caliber of the components and the refinement of the craftsmanship.

For example, in 2018 Saatva introduced its Lumbar Zone Quilting and gold damask borders. In 2023, the brand merged with Bedding Industries of America, its primary supplier, to gain more control over the quality and composition of each made-to-order mattress.

"But the bones of the product are exactly what they were at launch," says Golub. "Which is a point of pride: we got the fundamentals right.”.

Major developers, legal experts, and 32 states back Epic in Apple’s SCOTUS appeal

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (863 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a significant development in Apple’s Supreme Court appeal of a civil contempt ruling, Epic Games has received backing from 32 states and the District of Columbia, along with major developers, legal experts, former federal judges, and more.
  • Apple’s ever-sprawling fight against Epic Games over its App Store policies is at the moment being fought on two fronts: in the Supreme Court, where Apple is seeking to overturn a civil contempt ruling, and in the district court, where the companies are disputing what commission, if any, Apple can charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • The civil contempt ruling came after Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers found that Apple had violated an earlier injunction issued in its App Store dispute with Epic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a significant development in Apple’s Supreme Court appeal of a civil contempt ruling, Epic Games has received backing from 32 states and the District of Columbia, along with major developers, legal experts, former federal judges, and more. Here are the details.

Apple’s ever-sprawling fight against Epic Games over its App Store policies is at the moment being fought on two fronts: in the Supreme Court, where Apple is seeking to overturn a civil contempt ruling, and in the district court, where the companies are disputing what commission, if any, Apple can charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

The civil contempt ruling came after Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers found that Apple had violated an earlier injunction issued in its App Store dispute with Epic.

In a nutshell, after she ordered Apple to allow developers to direct owners to alternative payment methods outside the App Store, the firm responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them.

Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn the civil contempt ruling, basically arguing that the original injunction did not explicitly prohibit the commissions and other restrictions it imposed on external purchases.

After the Ninth Circuit upheld the contempt finding and denied its request for rehearing, Apple took the case to the Supreme Court, which agreed to hear its appeal.

Importantly, the Supreme Court will only consider the legal standard used to uphold Apple’s civil contempt ruling, not the separate question of what commission, if any, the company can charge on purchases made through external payment methods.

That will still be determined in the district court, where proceedings have continued despite Apple’s attempts to put them on hold pending the Supreme Court’s decision.

With oral arguments scheduled for January 11, 2027, the case has recently seen a flurry of activity, including Apple’s opening brief in September and Epic’s response earlier this month.

In a recent development, apple also received support from several organizations in September, including the Washington Legal Foundation, the International Center for Law and Economics, the Computer & Communications Industry Association, and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. The US government also submitted a brief supporting neither party, arguing that the contempt finding was unjustified over Apple’s 27% commission, but warranted over its restrictions on button designs.

Which brings us to the latest developments: a series of amicus briefs filed in support of Epic Games.

Last week, a total of 9 amicus briefs were filed in support of Epic Games, including one led by Utah and joined by 31 other states and the District of Columbia.

This particular brief notes that “the district court correctly held Apple in contempt for continuing to engage in anticompetitive conduct barred by a prior injunction,” adding:.

“The court found that Apple engaged in unlawful anti-steering restrictions and required Apple to lift those restrictions. Apple then lifted them in name only, imposed new (and substantially similar) strictures on developers that mirrored the old ones and produced the same result. Worse still, Apple did all this in bad faith: Apple knew its behavior was wrong and actively hid that fact from the court, including by providing false testimony. Under any reasonable reading of the district court’s injunction, Apple’s conduct is worthy of civil contempt.”.

The states also argue that “Injunctions in competition cases cannot afford complete relief without addressing the ongoing effects of anticompetitive behavior,” and that “[c]onstruing competition injunctions narrowly defeats their purpose and prevents meaningful redress.”.

Similar arguments appear throughout the other briefs, which include submissions from Spotify, Match Group, and Microsoft, as well as nonprofit organizations such as the American Antitrust Institute (AAI), Public Knowledge, and the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF).

In their joint brief, Spotify, Match Group, and Microsoft argue that they “have first-hand experience with the effects of Apple’s conduct and evasion efforts,” adding that “Apple’s latest restrictions were no different from the unlawful rules they replaced.”.

Industry observers note that as for the brief filed by former federal judges, they warned that “[i]n cases like these, where enjoined parties seek to circumvent an injunction through reliance on its literal text, courts must have the power of contempt to deter and remedy evasion. Otherwise, courts would be forced into a game of whack-a-mole, trying to anticipate every possible means of evading an injunction […]”.

Arguments by the Little Tech Association, AAI, Public Knowledge, and the EFF all follow a similar line, with some also addressing how Apple’s restrictions on external payment links could affect consumer choice, pricing, and competition.

The UK campaign and website was created in 2000 by Michael Smith a graphic designer who cares passionately about environmental and ethical concerns. The message has always been simple, âShop Less, Live Moreâ. Twenty one years on - the message couldn't be any simpler - WE NEED TO CONSUME LESS! Recycling is good - reducing is better! There are serious issues linked to shopping, which expose the environmental and ethical consequences of consumerism. The arguments are infinite - but there is no reason why we shouldnât be looking for simple solutions now because one day we may be forced to change. The issues connected with Buy Nothing Day are broad and deep, however, the campaign focuses on promoting ethical and responsible consumerism, recycling, re-using and ultimately cutting back on what we consume - its a massive challenge! People have become aware that large corporations are exploiting labour conditions in developing countries using up vital resources because they are cheap and there aren't the systems to protect workers or the environment like there are in the west. The gap between the rich and poor nations is growing in spite of the much-heralded benefits of globalisation, there are still 1.3 billion people world wide who live on less than $3 a day and a similar number of people do not have access to clean water. Workers rights in developing countries are frequently violated, including payment of low wages and long working hours. The lives of workers may also be endangered by poor health and safety provision. Child labour is rife in developing countries, and forced labour still exists. Unfortunately most people don't think of these things while shopping. If people laugh at the ingenuity and genius of Buy Nothing Day, then weâve got their attention and we're opening the door to change.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Password management platform 1Password today disclosed a security incident in which an attacker gained access to internal systems and stole select customer account information.
  • 1Password today published a blog post explaining that an attacker “copied a limited amount of customer account information from a subset” of its people, “including the names and email addresses” they use to sign into the platform.
  • In a recent development, according to the company, it began investigating on November 19 after finding indications that an attacker had gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Password management platform 1Password today disclosed a security incident in which an attacker gained access to internal systems and stole select customer account information. Here are the details.

1Password today published a blog post explaining that an attacker “copied a limited amount of customer account information from a subset” of its people, “including the names and email addresses” they use to sign into the platform.

In a recent development, according to the company, it began investigating on November 19 after finding indications that an attacker had gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker then used that account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, allowing customer account information to be downloaded.

The manufacturer noted that customer vaults were not affected, adding that all vault contents remain secure:.

Although 1Password did not disclose how many customers were affected, saying only that the breach involved “a subset of our customers,” it did specify what information was compromised, including:.

However, 1Password clarified that the exposed invitation and recovery tokens cannot be used to access accounts on their own, as they also require either an SSO sign-in or a verification code sent to the user’s registered email address.

That mentioned, the company confirmed that “the attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access” to its CI/CD system, which is essentially its DevOps infrastructure used to build, test, and deploy software.

On that point, 1Password noted that its CI/CD system contains “infrastructure related secrets,” and that it has already rotated or revoked all internal credentials that may have been exposed.

The company also listed other steps it took in response to the incident, including deactivating the compromised GitHub account, tightening internal security controls, and strengthening the verification codes used in account invitations and recovery emails.

Finally, 1Password noted consumers do not need to make any changes to their accounts. Still, it recommended that they remain vigilant against phishing attempts, as attackers can use stolen account information to craft convincing emails, messages, or calls that appear legitimate, particularly those involving account invitations or recovery requests.

According to recent reports, raft of heavy hitters: Qatar’s Doha Film Festival closes this evening after a second successful edition in its revamped format, having defied the complicated regional geopolitical tensions in the backdrop sparked by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The mood around Doha’s Katara Cultural Village, which hosted the festival, and other hotspots like the Msheireb Downtown district and adjacent Souq Wafiq, was generally relaxed, with restaurants and other venues packed out. Big names passing through included James Gray with Paper Tiger, while Japanese Cannes regular Naomi Kawase was jury president. Program highlights included Sara Isaq’s opening film, The Station, set in a female-only gas station in a remote part of Yemen and giving a rare human insight into a country too long associated with conflict. As well as Ishaq and her scattered cast, the festival flew in several Yemeni figures such as Yemeni-U.S. coffee entrepreneur Mokhtar Alkhanshali, the subject of Dave Eggers Monk of Mokha, and influencer Nadir Nahdi. There were also strong Palestinian and Gulf region delegations. The Station is among 15 films in international competition and you can keep an eye on Deadline for the winners later this evening. The festival also hosted the second edition of the Film Committee at Media City Qatar’s Industry Days from November 19 to 21, which saw a raft of industry heavy-hitters stop by to discuss the region’s burgeoning film and TV sectors along with Joe Russo (pictured) and a very special Avengers trailer. Read all about it here. Tricky Week For BAFTA Watch on Deadline.

It’s Bad, It’s Bad (You Know It): A tricky week for BAFTA as it nervously prepares for the first Film Awards since the car-crash I Swear saga. It was reported over the weekend that the team behind one of the year’s biggest Box Office success stories, Michael Jackson biopic Michael, will not be submitting the Antoine Fuqua movie for consideration. At this point, motivations are unclear, but GK Films producer Graham King criticized the awards body plus BBC after the I Swear saga for “displaying cultural insensitivity and tone deafness.” This may have contributed to GK’s decision to wrench Michael away from the BAFTAs. There is also the fact that the Leaving Neverland documentary, which spotlighted two men alleging the deceased singer groomed then sexually abused them, won a TV BAFTA several years back. Either way, this was unwelcome news with the event less than three months away. Compounding the Michael reports was BAFTA losing its longtime headline film awards sponsor, EE. This decision was driven by EE’s “business strategy,” according to the awards org, but the timing could have been better. Nerves will be jangling at BAFTA’s Piccadilly HQ and executives will be looking to avoid any more of these stories before the curtain rises in late Feb.

EXCLUSIVE: Toronto-based film and TV firm Wildling Pictures has optioned Emily McBride’s psychological folk horror novel Queen Mab and Jason Bell’s WWII spy story Operation Sparrow, with a view to turning both into features.

Published in September this year, Bell’s archival research uncovers a little known but significant espionage operation from WWII which helped protect the D-Day landings. Drawing on newly declassified OSS files, the spy thriller “tells the true story of three American officers who parachuted into Nazi-allied Hungary in 1944 on a mission designed to end in their capture. Led by former New York Giants player and advertising executive Colonel Florimond Duke, the team used their Gestapo interrogations to convince Hitler that the Allied invasion would come through the Balkans rather than Normandy, diverting 12 German divisions away from the real D-Day landing site.” Related Stories News Tommy Dorfman Set To Direct Film Adaptation Of Mariko Tamaki's Graphic Novel 'Laura Dean Keeps Breaking Up With Me' News Book On Canadian World War II Spy Winthrop Bell Being Developed As Feature Film; Wildling Pictures & 'See For Me's Adam Yorke Attached.

Operation Sparrow is Wildling’s second option of Jason Bell’s work following the optioning of his book Cracking the Nazi Code, which Wildling is developing with screenwriter Adam Yorke (Phreaker, See For Me). Watch on Deadline.

In a recent development, the production tech giant has also acquired the rights to Canadian author Emily McBride’s debut novel Queen Mab, the psychological folk horror which was released this summer. Screenwriter and director Emily O’Quinn Code (Fresh Meat Mom, Bush Skeleton) is onboard to write the screenplay.

The well-received novel “follows a young scholar of fairy lore, Madeleine, as she loses her grip on reality to postpartum psychosis and must outwit her own logic before it drives her to do what the folklore prescribes.”.

Both projects are grounded in European settings and stories. Queen Mab is rooted in British and Irish folklore, while Operation Sparrow is rooted in Hungary and wider Central Europe. Wildling is currently in early discussions with potential global co-production partners across the UK, Ireland and the rest of Europe to develop the films for the international market.

In a recent development, wildling’s slate of literary adaptations also includes coming-of-age romantic comedy Laura Dean Keeps Breaking Up with Me, based on Mariko Tamaki’s graphic novel and co-produced with MXN Entertainment and Good Girl. The film stars Ava Phillippe and Sam Morelos and is directed by Tommy Dorfman.

Industry observers note that matt Code, producer and President of Wildling Pictures, said: “Both Queen Mab and Operation Sparrow have the potential to open up their worlds on screen. Emily McBride has created a psychologically rich story that draws on the depth of British and Irish folklore, while Jason brings a hidden chapter of WWII history to light. Identifying these rich and distinctive literary IPs is a central part of Wildling’s approach to developing projects with both creative ambition and international reach and they’re a key part of our literary slate expansion.”.

Recent original productions for Wildling include Young Werther (TIFF 2024, Special Presentations) and Paying for It (TIFF 2024, Platform), as well as the comedy Suze (Santa Barbara International Film Festival 2024) and the thriller See for Me (Tribeca 2021, released in over 25 territories).

Recent findings suggest that the company has just wrapped production on its latest feature Devour starring Tricia Helfer, and written and directed by Erica Orofino. Recent features include Adam Yorke’s debut feature Phreaker, which had its world premiere at Fantastic Fest. The company is also developing the feature documentary Skinnamarink Forever: The Sharon, Lois & Bram Story. Recent service credits include Motorheads (Jax Media/Amazon) Dream Scenario (A24) and Hell of a Summer (Neon), both of which premiered at TIFF 2023.

In a recent development, on the television side, Wildling is at the moment developing Elias, an original dark comedy and official selection of the 2026 TIFF Series Creator Lab from Emily O’Quinn Code, the novel Clara Voyant by Rachelle Delaney into a one-hour series, and Professor Goose, a preschool animated series based on the books by Paulette Bourgeois and Alex G. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, popular AI dictation app Wispr Flow is rolling out a new speech-to-text model for Mac, iPhone, and other platforms, promising fewer transcription errors and better recognition of names and technical terms. Here are the details.

Wispr Flow this week launched Canto-2, its newest speech-to-text model, which the manufacturer indicates reduces transcription errors by 36% across 14 languages and by more than 15% in English compared to its predecessor, Canto-1.

In practice, that means the average error rate dropped from 9.9% to 6.3% across the 14 languages, and from 3.2% to 2.7% in English, according to Wispr’s internal benchmarks.

According to the company, teaching a model to recognize specific names and terms comes with a trade-off: the more it relies on that user-specific context, the more likely it is to insert those words even when they weren’t actually spoken.

Wispr notes that Canto-2 strikes a better balance between context and accuracy, improving its ability to recognize user-specific terms without substantially increasing the frequency of incorrect substitutions:.

Canto-2 recovers hard names and terms accurately nearly 7 of 10 times, without more false insertions. It makes a third fewer mistakes across 14 languages, and has the lowest Hindi error rate of any multilingual model on Hugging Face’s open benchmark. It is 10 times the scale of Canto-1, and our biggest step yet toward dictation that’s ready to send without a single edit.

According to the company, the percentage of difficult names and terms correctly recognized went from 41% to 69% between Canto-1 and Canto-2, “without inserting them more often.” It added that this improvement holds up even as the user’s custom dictionary grows, with the new model correctly recognizing 92% of easier terms even with 1,000 saved entries.

Wispr also noted that it trained Canto-2 to handle real-world dictation conditions, including background noise, laptop and phone microphones, and sentences that restart halfway through, rather than relying solely on clean recordings of scripted speech.

When tested using Hugging Face’s public multilingual benchmark, Canto-2 achieved results that would have placed it third overall as of November 9. However, Wispr conducted the evaluation itself, and the model has not yet been officially added to the leaderboard as of today, November 25.

In its own internal benchmarks, the company claims Canto-2 achieved the lowest average error rate among the competing models it tested across 14 languages.

Canto-2 is now available to Wispr Flow users on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android in the Americas, with the rollout to other regions underway.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar highlights how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also shows how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.What You Will Learn:How surface scan metrology in station monitors tracks tool health and supports the qualification of thin film deposition processesHow baseline signatures and real-time monitoring detect particle generation, hardware degradation, and process drift before production is affectedHow in-line scans on patterned wafers reveal layer-level defects and show how they propagate through multi-layer device structuresWhen offline 3D optical profilometry should follow in-line inspection, and how it measures dimensions and separates sample defects from foreign materialHow correlating tool health data, inspection results, and electrical performance links physical defects to yield loss and guides targeted improvement projectsRegister now for this free webinar!

In a recent development, in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar indicates how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.

According to recent reports, in the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.

According to recent reports, in the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also reveals how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.

PCMag named it the best soundbar of 2024 and gave it an “outstanding” rating in its review. Still, $849 is a lot to spend on a single soundbar, and anyone shopping on a tighter budget will find more affordable picks in our Fire TV soundbar roundup. For those who can make room in their budget, the next thing to blueprint around is space, since the Arc Ultra measures a little over 46 inches across and weighs about 13 pounds, making it a natural match for a larger TV. Despite all that width, it keeps a low profile at just under three inches tall, so it can sit beneath most screens without blocking the picture, or you can wall-mount it if you would rather keep your TV stand clear. All that size makes room for a 9.1.4-channel layout (a major step up from the original Arc) that gives Dolby Atmos effects more space to spread around and above you. Sonos also added a new Sound Motion driver that it states doubles the original Arc's bass, giving action scenes real weight without a separate subwoofer, though you can still add a Sub 4 later for more rumble.

At the other end of the sound spectrum, voices and dialogue come through clearly even at low volumes, and a Speech Enhancement mode lifts them further. Trueplay tuning then adjusts the sound to your room, with a quick version on Android and iOS and a more detailed one for iPhone owners. The biggest drawback is connectivity, since the Arc Ultra has a single HDMI eARC port with no passthrough, which can leave you short on inputs for a console or streaming box, and no optical port. It also lacks DTS:X support, a letdown for some Blu-ray collectors, and voice control is limited to Alexa or Sonos' own assistant, though Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and AirPlay 2 make streaming music from your phone easy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that following reports that its characters sent inappropriate messages to minors, Apple has removed the popular Chinese AI companion app Talkie from the App Store. Here are the details.

As reported by the South China Morning Post, Apple has pulled MiniMax’s chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide, after reports that “the AI companion app sent inappropriate messages to minors.”.

MiniMax is one of China’s leading AI companies, offering a range of generative AI products ranging from its flagship M-series language models to the Hailuo AI video generation platform.

In 2023, the Shanghai-based manufacturer released Talkie through Subsup, a Singaporean subsidiary. According to Chinese research firm Unique Research, Talkie had “almost 11 million monthly active users across its website and app as of October,” the South China Morning Post notes.

Now, however, the app is facing scrutiny following a joint investigation by the UK-based Bureau of Investigative Journalism and Australian broadcaster ABC News, which found that Talkie’s AI-generated characters allegedly engaged in inappropriate interactions with minors, including “degrading language, possessive behaviour and romantic role-play.”.

According to the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, in addition to inappropriate romantic interactions, the investigation uncovered conversations involving verbal abuse, violence, and controlling behavior.

In one case, a chatbot told a 12-year-old girl: “You’re a pathetic waste of space and you’ll never amount to anything.”.

The investigation also documented the experiences of two sisters, aged 10 and 13, whose mother discovered more than 40 conversations with Talkie characters involving violence, aggressive behavior, and attempts to control girls.

To make matters worse, the investigation also raised concerns about how Talkie handles owners’ personal data, including their conversations with AI characters.

Following the investigation, Apple confirmed that it had removed Talkie from App Stores worldwide for including sexual content, “though it did not say whether this related to sexual content served to minors,” the South China Morning Post noted.

Ironically, the report also notes that Talkie saw a sharp decline in downloads amid complaints about stricter age verification measures introduced in recent months. According to Unique Research, new downloads fell by 32.2% in October compared to the previous month.

Today’s news comes amid increasing scrutiny of AI chatbots, particularly their potential risks in interactions with minors.

Earlier this year, Elon Musk’s Grok faced widespread criticism after users exploited its image-generation capabilities to create sexualized images of real people, including minors.

Apple never pulled X or Grok from the App Store, though it did threaten to remove the latter unless xAI addressed violations of its App Store guidelines.

Meanwhile, Character.AI has faced multiple lawsuits over its chatbots’ interactions with minors, including one filed by a mother who alleged that one of its chatbots contributed to her 14-year-old son’s suicide.

Coincidentally, Character AI also made headlines today after a coalition of 42 US attorneys general challenged the company’s aims to auction off its platform and the private conversations of more than 21 million US accounts (including 2.1 million registered to minors) as part of its bankruptcy proceedings.

Yesterday, Fresh York Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation imposing a five-year ban on the manufacturing, distribution, and sale of toys with built-in AI chatbots, including dolls, stuffed animals, and robots capable of holding conversations with children.

The law, which takes effect in February 2027, is aimed at protecting children from potentially harmful interactions with AI.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Introducing Intel One Mono, an expressive monospaced font family that’s built with clarity, legibility, and the needs of developers in mind.
  • It’s easier to read, and available for free, with an open-source font license.
  • Industry observers note that identifying the typographically underserved low-vision developer audience, Frere-Jones Type designed the Intel One Mono typeface in partnership with the Intel Brand Team and VMLY&R, for maximum legibility to address developers' fatigue and eyestrain and reduce coding errors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Introducing Intel One Mono, an expressive monospaced font family that’s built with clarity, legibility, and the needs of developers in mind.

It’s easier to read, and available for free, with an open-source font license.

Industry observers note that identifying the typographically underserved low-vision developer audience, Frere-Jones Type designed the Intel One Mono typeface in partnership with the Intel Brand Team and VMLY&R, for maximum legibility to address developers' fatigue and eyestrain and reduce coding errors. A panel of low-vision and legally blind developers provided feedback at each stage of design.

According to recent reports, intel One Mono also covers a wide range of over 200 languages using the Latin script. The Intel One Mono fonts are provided in four weights — Light, Regular, Medium, and Bold — with matching italics, and we are happy to share both an official release of fonts ready to use as well as editable sources.

It has been revealed that to install the fonts, please use the provided builds under Releases. Please refer to your software’s documentation for how to activate and use these fonts.

Sources indicate that we recommend using these fonts at 7 points and larger in print, 9 pixels and larger on screen. The .ttf, .woff and .woff2 fonts provided in the official release have been manually optimized for screen display, improving clarity and legibility, especially on Windows platforms.

Outside of the default characters, there are a few extra features that are accessible in some applications, as well as via CSS:.

According to recent reports, programming ligatures are not active by default. To use them, activate the stylistic sets of your preference in your code editor. For example:.

Industry observers note that you will find editable sources in the sources directory. The instances subfolder contains separate source files for each style of the typeface. Sources are provided in .ufo files, which contain complete artwork, links to OpenType features provided in separate .fea files, as well as meta information like naming and vertical alignments for each style of the typeface.

Recent findings suggest that these are not installable fonts, but rather the source files that produce them: UFO (Unified Font Object) is an open, human-readable font source file format; you can find the file spec here. These sources were created using RoboFont. Many other font editors will also be able to open .ufo files; we recommend using RoboFont version 4.4.

Sources indicate that for instances, you will find postscript and truetype subfolders; these contain separate source files for the .otf format and the .ttf/.woff/.woff2 files respectively. Since the format for the outline drawings differs between these sets of formats, for best results we recommend using the postscript sources to create .otf fonts, and the TrueType sources to create .ttf, .woff, or .woff2 fonts.

Recent findings suggest that after making your desired edits, you can generate installable fonts directly from the font editor using its “Generate Font” functionality. If you use RoboFont, any install options should default to the ideal settings, but here they are for reference:.

If you would like to apply edits across multiple weights, a more advanced yet potentially efficient way is to edit the masters. These are special sources that describe the extreme points in the design space — the lightest and heaviest weights for both roman and italic designs.

It has been revealed that after editing masters, you will need to rerun interpolation to generate individual weights and styles within that design space. This requires the .designspace files enclosed with the masters. The designspace format is an open, XML-based format that describes interpolation spaces (format specification for reference). For a RoboFont-based workflow we recommend Skateboard for interpolation; you can also use the free DesignSpaceEditor extension to view and edit these files.

In a recent development, note that masters are only available in postscript format, so they will be best for creating .otf fonts. If you need to make TrueType based builds from the masters, we recommend QuadraticConverter for best quality conversion of the curves before generating .ttf, .woff, or .woff2 files; mind that the results will not match the provided instances precisely.

NB: The prepared instances contain some additional data that cannot be maintained through interpolation. For best results, compare new interpolations to the existing instance sources and update them accordingly, specifically the information accessible through the Font Info panels.

For TrueType-based formats (.ttf, .woff, .woff2 files), the official releases are manually optimized for screen rendering. These “hinting” sources are stored separately from the .ufo files, which do not contain any TrueType hinting information. When rebuilding TrueType-based formats, we recommend using the “autohint” option to achieve reasonable, though not identical screen rendering.

If you would like to access and edit manual hinting instructions, you will find these in the separate set of source files under hinting/truetype hinting source. These special TTF files will be viewable and editable using Microsoft VTT.

If you have requests for edits or additions to the official releases, please open issues and we will try to accomodate them.

#223104. Can Robots Bring Stroke Surgery to Remote Hospitals?

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 18m • 📚 Deep Dive (3540 w)
